27.s: If the deficiency of a particular year's rainfall exceeds 50% of normal, it is termed as
27.x: IMD: a rainfall deficiency of 26-50% of normal is moderate drought and more than 50% is severe drought; there is no separate 'extreme' category.

27.s: What is drought?
o: A prolonged deficiency of rainfall or moisture leading to water scarcity
A permanent change in the course of a river
A sudden excess of rainfall causing widespread flooding
A short-term rise in groundwater levels after rainfall
27.x: Drought is a long shortage of rain or moisture that leads to water scarcity. A sudden excess of rain is a flood.
n: Drought is a prolonged deficiency of rainfall or moisture leading to water scarcity. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Drought is a serious shortfall in the availability of water. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
xs: Drought is **a prolonged deficiency of rainfall or moisture leading to water scarcity** — option **(1)**.
It is a **serious shortfall** in the **availability of water**.
A **sudden excess of rainfall** causing flooding describes a **flood**, not drought.
xa: Drought is **slow-onset** — a **creeping emergency** or **creeping hazard**.
It mainly affects **agriculture**, **drinking-water supply** and **industry**.
**Normal SW-monsoon rainfall:** **868.6 mm** (**1971-2020** base).
**Drought** nodal ministry: **Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**.

27.s: What aggravates severe groundwater depletion in drought-prone Rayalaseema?
27.x: Rayalaseema faces monsoon failure, crop loss, distress migration and severe groundwater depletion, aggravated by deep borewells.
xa: **Rayalaseema drought** is one of AP's three hazards, with **coastal cyclones** and **delta floods**.
Other drought-prone regions: Western Rajasthan, Kutch-Saurashtra, Marathwada-Vidarbha, interior Karnataka.
Hazard → region: **drought** → **Rajasthan + Deccan interior**.

27.s: Which of the following is NOT listed among the drought-prone regions of India?
27.x: Lower Assam is flood-prone (Brahmaputra plains), not drought-prone. The drought-prone regions listed are western Rajasthan, Kutch-Saurashtra, Marathwada-Vidarbha, interior Karnataka and Rayalaseema.
27.tq: Find the geographically misplaced region in a regional classification.
xs: **Lower Assam** is not a drought-prone region — so option **(2)** is correct.
Assam is **flood-prone**: **31.05 lakh ha** of flood-prone area, in the **Brahmaputra-Ganga plains** flood belt.
**Interior Karnataka, Western Rajasthan and Kutch-Saurashtra** are listed drought-prone regions.
xa: Others listed: **Marathwada-Vidarbha** and **Rayalaseema** (AP).
Hazard → region: **drought** → **Rajasthan + Deccan interior**.
About **68%** of cultivable area is drought-vulnerable.

27.s: What is a drought defined by rainfall falling below the long-period average called?
27.x: A rainfall decline below the long-period average defines meteorological drought; ecological drought involves collapsing ecosystem productivity.
xa: **Hydrological** drought: fall in surface and groundwater after prolonged deficiency.
**Agricultural** drought: soil-moisture deficit causing crop failure.
Drought effects include **land degradation**, desertification and **ecosystem damage**.

27.s: Which of the following ocean-atmosphere conditions can trigger drought in India?
27.x: El Nino, along with irregular or delayed monsoon, monsoon breaks and high temperature and evaporation, can trigger drought.
xa: Normal SW-monsoon rainfall: **868.6 mm** (**1971-2020** base).
About **68%** of the cultivable area is drought-vulnerable.
Drought-prone: Western Rajasthan, Kutch-Saurashtra, Marathwada-Vidarbha, interior Karnataka, **Rayalaseema**.

27.s: Which of the following pairs (type of drought – meaning) is correctly matched?
o: Hydrological – Soil-moisture deficit causing crop failure
Agricultural – Fall in surface and groundwater
Socio-economic – Water and food shortage hitting livelihoods and markets
Agricultural – Water and food shortage hitting livelihoods
27.x: Socio-economic drought is water and food shortage hitting livelihoods and markets; hydrological drought is the fall in surface and groundwater, and agricultural drought is a soil-moisture deficit causing crop failure.
xa: **Meteorological** drought = rainfall well below the **long-period average** over a period.
**Ecological** drought = ecosystem productivity collapses.
About **68%** of cultivable area is drought-vulnerable.

27.s: Which one of the following is NOT a long-term consequence of recurrent droughts?
o: A sustained increase in farm output
27.x: Droughts generally reduce farm output; they contribute to groundwater depletion, land degradation, desertification and distress migration.
27.tq: Identify the reversed trend in a list of long-term consequences.
xs: **A sustained increase in farm output** is not a drought effect — so option **(3)** is correct.
Droughts cause **lower farm output**, not higher.
The real long-term effects are **groundwater depletion**, **land degradation and desertification** and **rural (distress) migration**.
xa: Drought also brings **rural indebtedness** and **ecosystem damage**.
In **Rayalaseema**, **deep borewells** cause severe groundwater depletion.
About **68%** of the cultivable area is drought-vulnerable.

27.s: Meteorological drought is associated with a rainfall deficiency of at least how much of the long-period average?
27.x: Meteorological drought means rain at least 25% below the long-period average.
n: Meteorological drought is indicated by a rainfall deficiency of at least 25% from the long-period average. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Socio-economic drought occurs when demand for water exceeds supply. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Socio-economic drought causes social and economic stress. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
xa: **Agricultural** drought: **soil moisture insufficient** for crop growth.
**Hydrological** drought: depletion of **reservoirs**, **rivers**, **aquifers**.
**Ecological** drought: ecosystem productivity collapses.

27.s: Which of the following pairs (type of drought – time lag) is INCORRECTLY matched?
27.x: Hydrological drought appears after a delay of weeks to months; it is meteorological drought that shows up at once.
n: Meteorological drought has an immediate time lag. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Agricultural drought has an intermediate time lag. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Hydrological drought has a delayed time lag of weeks to months. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Socio-economic drought has a long-term time lag. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
xa: Meteorological drought: rainfall at least **25%** below the **long-period average**.
Hydrological drought hits **surface-water** and **groundwater sources**.
**Drought-prone:** Western Rajasthan, Kutch-Saurashtra, Marathwada-Vidarbha, interior Karnataka, **Rayalaseema**.

27.s: What is the drought in which water demand exceeds supply and shortages hit livelihoods and markets called?
27.x: Socio-economic drought arises when demand exceeds supply and shortages hit livelihoods and markets; it has the longest time lag.

27.s: As per IMD, what is a rainfall deficiency of 26–50% of the long-period average termed?
27.x: IMD treats a 26–50% deficiency as moderate drought and over 50% as severe drought.

27.s: What is the normal South-West monsoon rainfall of India (1971-2020 average)?
27.x: IMD's normal (LPA) for SW-monsoon rain over 1971-2020 is 868.6 mm.

27.s: With which of the following is salinity intrusion, a secondary hazard, mainly associated?
27.x: Coastal floods bring salinity intrusion; cloudbursts trigger flash floods and river floods cause bank erosion.
n: A cloudburst causes a flash flood as a secondary hazard. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A flash flood causes a landslide as a secondary hazard. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A river flood causes bank erosion as a secondary hazard. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A coastal flood causes salinity intrusion as a secondary hazard. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A cloudburst causes flash floods. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: **Flash flood → landslide**; **urban flood → traffic or infrastructure collapse**.
**Flood → water contamination**, **disease risk**, **crop or livelihood loss**.
**Rapid-onset:** cyclone, flood, tsunami; **slow-onset:** drought.

27.s: Which of the following pairs (flood type – typical impact) is correctly matched?
o: Dam failure – Drought in the downstream area
27.x: Cloudbursts on steep slopes trigger landslides (and flash floods). River floods mainly damage crops on floodplains, urban floods disrupt infrastructure, and dam failure causes catastrophic downstream flooding, not drought.
n: A river flood causes crop damage. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
An urban flood disrupts infrastructure. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A cloudburst causes landslides. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A dam failure causes catastrophic downstream flooding. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]

27.s: What is a flood in which river discharge exceeds channel capacity called?
27.x: A river flood is discharge exceeding the channel; a flash flood is sudden intense runoff and an urban flood is rain with poor drainage.
n: A river flood occurs when river discharge exceeds channel capacity. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A flash flood involves sudden high-intensity runoff or discharge. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
An urban flood results from rainfall combined with inadequate urban drainage. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A drought is a prolonged water deficit. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: **Cloudburst:** extremely intense localized rainfall → **flash floods** and **landslides**.
**Dam failure:** sudden water release → **catastrophic downstream flooding**.
**Coastal flooding:** **storm surge**, tidal or wave action on a **low-lying coast** → inundation, **salinity**.
**Drought** is **slow-onset** — a **creeping emergency**.

27.s: What mainly causes coastal floods?
o: Storm surge, cyclones and high tides
27.x: Coastal floods come from storm surge, cyclones and high tides; GLOFs come from bursting glacial lakes.
n: Riverine or fluvial floods result from the overflow of rivers due to heavy monsoon rainfall. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Urban floods result from poor drainage, heavy rain, and encroachment on wetlands. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Coastal floods result from storm surges, cyclones, and high tides. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Glacial Lake Outburst Floods result from the bursting of glacial lakes. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
xa: GLOF-prone: **Himalayan states** — **Uttarakhand**, **Sikkim**.
Riverine floods hit the **Ganga**, **Brahmaputra**, **Kosi** and **Godavari** basins.
Flash floods: **sudden intense rainfall** or **cloudbursts** in **Himalayan regions** and **urban areas**.

27.s: Besides inundation, what does coastal flooding commonly cause?
27.x: Storm surge, tides or waves on a low coast cause coastal floods, which bring both inundation and salinity.
n: Coastal flooding results from storm surge, tidal action, or wave action affecting a low-lying coast. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Coastal flooding causes inundation. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Coastal flooding causes salinity. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: **Coastal flood → salinity intrusion** (secondary hazard).
A **cyclone** produces a **storm surge**; a **high tide** gives a **higher baseline water level**.
**Sea-level rise** increases coastal exposure; a **low-lying delta** suffers **greater inundation**.

27.s: Which of the following can a cloudburst most likely cause?
27.x: A cloudburst dumps very intense rain on a small area, so runoff surges and causes a flash flood.
n: A cloudburst consists of extremely intense localized rainfall. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A cloudburst produces very intense rainfall over a small area. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Cloudbursts are highly localized. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Cloudbursts are extremely intense. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Cloudbursts produce rapid runoff. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Cloudbursts have strong flash-flood potential. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A cloudburst causes flash floods. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: **IMD:** at least **100 mm (10 cm)** in **one hour** over about **20–30 square kilometres**.
Cloudbursts mostly occur at **1,000 to 2,500 metres** in mountains.
Ordinary heavy rainfall may **cover a larger area** and be **prolonged**; its runoff **depends on duration and intensity**.
**Flash flood → Landslide** is the next link in the secondary-hazard chain.

27.s: Which of the following reduces urban flooding?
27.x: Restoring wetlands reduces urban flooding because wetlands store water; wetland loss, paved surfaces and blocked drains add to it.
n: Encroachment of drains causes urban flooding. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Wetland destruction causes urban flooding. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Impervious surfaces cause urban flooding. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Wetland protection preserves natural storage. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Wetlands store excess water. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: Other urban-flood causes: **poor storm-water drainage**, **unplanned urbanisation**, **floodplain construction**.
**Urban green infrastructure** increases **infiltration** and reduces **runoff**.
**Prep:** unplanned **concretisation**, blocked drains/canals, **encroached lakes**.
Urban-flood cities: **Mumbai**, **Chennai**, **Bengaluru**, **Hyderabad**, **Delhi**.

27.s: Which of the following can cause urban flooding?
27.x: Floodplain construction, like poor storm drains, unplanned growth, low ground and high tides, causes urban flooding.
n: Poor storm-water drainage causes urban flooding. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
High tides or storm surge cause urban flooding. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Unplanned urbanisation causes urban flooding. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Low-lying terrain causes urban flooding. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Floodplain construction causes urban flooding. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: Other causes: **intense rainfall**, **cloudbursts**, **cyclone rainfall**, **encroachment of drains**, **wetland destruction**.
Major urban floods: **Mumbai 2005** (**944 mm** in **24 hours**), **Chennai 2015**.
**AP City Flood Alert:** **48-hour rainfall** forecasts + **6-hour flash-flood** warnings.

27.s: With which river is urban flooding in Vijayawada associated?
27.x: Vijayawada's urban flooding is linked to the Budameru rivulet.
xa: Urban flood causes: **unplanned concretisation**, blocked drains, encroached lakes and extreme rainfall.
**AP City Flood Alert** uses satellite **DEM** plus ~**30 years** of Budameru data.
It gives **48-hour rainfall** forecasts and **6-hour flash-flood** warnings.

27.s: Where is Andhra Pradesh's AI-based City Flood Alert platform (July 2026) to be implemented first?
27.x: It starts in Vijayawada (using Budameru data) and later covers all ULBs; it was built by RTGS and APSDMA with IIT Gandhinagar.
xa: It uses **satellite DEM** plus about **30 years** of **Budameru** data.
**Vijayawada** floods come from the **Budameru rivulet**; Visakhapatnam and Guntur are other AP flood cities.
Urban floods come under the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**.

27.s: What caused the major 2008 Bihar flood in the Kosi region?
27.x: Bihar's 2008 flood happened because the Kosi embankment breached.
n: Bihar experienced a major flood in 2008. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
An embankment breach caused the 2008 Bihar flood in the Kosi region. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
xa: **Assam** and **Bihar** are the **worst-affected** flood states.
The **Kosi** basin is a **riverine flood** basin with the **Ganga**, **Brahmaputra**, **Godavari**.
Other major floods: **Mumbai 2005**, **Kedarnath 2013**, **Chennai 2015**, **Kerala 2018**.

27.s: About how much rain fell in 24 hours before the Mumbai flood of 26 July 2005?
27.x: Mumbai received 944 mm in 24 hours on 26 July 2005, and its drainage failed.

27.s: What mainly aggravated the Chennai flood of December 2015?
27.x: Chennai's 2015 flood came from extreme rain worsened by wetland destruction; the Kosi flood was an embankment breach and Kerala 2018 involved dam releases.

27.s: Besides heavy rain, what caused the Kerala floods of August 2018?
27.x: The 2018 Kerala floods resulted from heavy rain and dam releases.

27.s: Which of the following can magnify the coastal-flooding impact of storm surges?
27.x: Sea-level rise magnifies storm-surge impacts and can cause permanent inundation of low-lying land.
xa: Cyclones affect **13 coastal states/UTs** and **84 coastal districts**.
The **east coast** gets far more cyclones than the west.
AP coast: **62+ cyclonic events** in four decades.

27.s: Which combination forms coastal defence against storm surges?
o: Check dams, contour bunds and farm ponds
Mangroves, shelter belts, dune stabilisation and seawalls
27.x: Mangroves and shelter belts anchor sediment and buffer storm surges, while dune stabilisation and seawalls strengthen coastal defence.
xa: Storm surge = abnormal sea-level rise from **cyclone winds + low pressure**.
Very high tsunami risk zone: **Andaman & Nicobar**.
AP faces **coastal cyclones, delta floods and Rayalaseema drought**.

27.s: In Andhra Pradesh's hydrological-disaster pattern, with which hazard is the Rayalaseema region mainly associated?
27.x: AP's coastal belt goes with cyclones and storm surges, the deltaic plains with floods and Rayalaseema with droughts.
xa: AP is the **most cyclone-prone state** — **62+ cyclonic events** in four decades.
**Krishna-Godavari** delta floods are worst when **Srisailam, Nagarjuna Sagar** or **Hirakud** release water together.
**Rayalaseema**: deep borewells → **severe groundwater depletion**.

27.s: Which of the following statements regarding coastal flooding is incorrect?
o: High tide creates a higher baseline water level.
Heavy coastal rainfall can cause drainage congestion.
Sea-level rise leads to lower coastal exposure.
27.x: Option C is incorrect: sea-level rise increases coastal exposure. High tides, heavy rain and cyclone surges all add to coastal flooding.
n: A cyclone produces a storm surge. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A high tide produces a higher baseline water level. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Heavy coastal rainfall causes drainage congestion. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Sea-level rise increases coastal exposure. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xs: **Sea-level rise leads to lower coastal exposure** is incorrect — option **(3)**; sea-level rise **increases** coastal exposure.
A **high tide** gives a **higher baseline water level**; **heavy coastal rainfall** causes **drainage congestion**.
A **cyclone** produces a **storm surge** — correct.
xa: **Storm surge:** abnormal sea-level rise pushed by **cyclone winds + low pressure**.
**Mangroves** with coastal shelter belts **buffer storm surges**.
**Salinity intrusion** hits **agriculture** and **water**.

27.s: Which agencies undertook the remeasurement that produced the revised coastline length?
o: India Meteorological Department with the Geological Survey of India
National Disaster Management Authority with the Indian Coast Guard
Central Water Commission with the Forest Survey of India
National Hydrographic Office with the Survey of India
27.x: The revised coastline was measured by the National Hydrographic Office in association with the Survey of India.
27.tq: Identify the correct institutional pair and avoid swapping neighbouring technical agencies.
xs: The coastline was remeasured by the **National Hydrographic Office** with the **Survey of India** — option **(4)**.
It was reported by the **MHA** in **Dec 2024** (remeasurement **2023-24**).
xa: New length **11,098.81 km**, up from **7,516.6 km** (+~**47.7%**) — **only the method changed**, not the land.
**Gujarat** is first (**2,340.62 km**); **Tamil Nadu** second; **AP** third (**1,053.07 km**).
**GSI** is the nodal agency for **landslide** studies — a different body.

27.s: Under the revised coastline figures (2023-24), what is the rank of Andhra Pradesh's coastline?
27.x: Andhra Pradesh (1,053.07 km) is third; Gujarat is first and Tamil Nadu second.

27.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about storm surges?
o: They are pushed by cyclone winds and low pressure
The west coast gets far more cyclones than the east
A high tide raises their baseline
27.x: The east coast, not the west, gets far more cyclones; the other statements are correct.

27.s: What is the length of India's coastline as remeasured by the National Hydrographic Office and reported in December 2024?
27.x: The 2023-24 remeasurement put India's coastline at 11,098.81 km, up from the old 7,516.6 km.

27.s: Which state has the longest coastline in India under the revised figures of 2024?
27.x: Gujarat ranks first (2,340.62 km), Tamil Nadu second and Andhra Pradesh third (1,053.07 km).

27.s: What is the coastline length of Andhra Pradesh as per the remeasured figures reported in December 2024?
27.x: The 2023-24 remeasurement gave AP 1,053.07 km, third after Gujarat (2,340.62 km) and Tamil Nadu.

27.s:
Construction of water shed structures at right places can be the mitigation action for which of the following disasters?
(i) Tornadoes (ii) Fire (iii) Drought (iv) Flood
27.x: Watershed structures (check dams, percolation tanks) store runoff for dry spells and slow floods, so they mitigate drought and flood – not tornadoes or fire. Moved.

27.s: Which technique is used for flood forecasting?
27.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
27.x: Flood forecasting uses GIS, radar and remote sensing; Richter measures earthquakes, Pascal is a pressure unit and MRI is medical imaging. Moved.

27.s: In which year did the 'Boxing Day Tsunami' take place?
27.src: APPSC Asst. B.C. Welfare Officers, Royalty Inspector
27.x: The Indian Ocean "Boxing Day" tsunami struck on 26 December 2004.

27.s: Which of the following state was not affected by the Tsunami that occurred in 2004?
27.x: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami struck Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry and the A&N Islands; Odisha's coast was not affected.

27.s: Which State is the most affected in India during the massive Tsunami that occurred in the year 2004?
27.src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
27.x: Tamil Nadu was the worst-affected Indian State in the December 2004 tsunami (Nagapattinam the worst district); Odisha, Goa and Karnataka were hardly affected.

27.s: What is a landslide?
o: Accumulation of soil and vegetation on flat agricultural land
Gradual movement of ocean water towards the coastline
Mass movement of rocks, debris or earth down mountain slopes or riverbanks
Sudden upward movement of rocks under the influence of gravity
27.x: A landslide is the mass movement of rock, debris or earth down a slope or riverbank under gravity. Option D wrongly says the movement is upward.
27.tq: Recall the definition of a landslide.
n: A landslide is the mass movement of rocks, debris, or earth down mountain slopes or riverbanks. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
A landslide is a rapid downward movement of rock, soil, debris, or vegetation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Gravity influences the downward movement in a landslide. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
xs: A landslide is the **mass movement of rocks, debris or earth down mountain slopes or riverbanks** — option **(3)**.
It is a **rapid downward movement** under the influence of **gravity** — not upward, as option (4) claims.
xa: It may occur **gradually** or **suddenly without warning**, mostly in **hilly regions**.
It is both a **geological** and a **hydro-meteorological** hazard.
About **12.6%** of India's land (about **0.42 million sq km**) is landslide-prone.

27.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Geological Survey of India is the nodal agency for landslides.
Approximately 12.6% of India's land area is landslide-prone.
The NDMA Guidelines on Management of Landslides and Snow Avalanches were issued in 2019.
Prolonged rainfall is a major rainfall trigger for landslides.
27.x: Option C is incorrect: NDMA's guidelines on landslides and snow avalanches came in 2009, not 2019. 2019 is the National Landslide Risk Management Strategy.
27.tq: Discriminate the 2009 guidelines from the 2019 strategy.
n: Prolonged rainfall is a major rainfall trigger for landslides. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Approximately 12.6% of India’s land area is landslide-prone. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
The NDMA document titled Guidelines on Management of Landslides and Snow Avalanches was issued in 2009. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
The Geological Survey of India (GSI) is an organisation associated with landslide forecasting. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Heavy rainfall is the main trigger for landslides in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
xs: **NDMA Guidelines on Landslides and Snow Avalanches issued in 2019** is incorrect — option **(3)**.
The **NDMA Guidelines** were issued in **2009**; the **National Landslide Risk Management Strategy** came in **2019**.
**GSI** is the **nodal agency**, about **12.6%** of land is landslide-prone, and **prolonged rainfall** is a major trigger — all correct.
xa: GSI runs the **National Landslide Susceptibility Mapping programme**.
**National Landslide Forecasting Centre** is a key initiative.
**Recent major event:** **Wayanad**, **Kerala** — **2024**.

27.s:
Assertion (A): A landslide is a geological hazard.
Reason (R): A landslide is a hydro-meteorological hazard.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
27.x: Both are true: a landslide is both a geological and a hydro-meteorological hazard. One label does not explain the other, so R does not explain A.
27.tq: Ask whether two labels explain each other.
n: A landslide is a geological hazard. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
A landslide is a hydro-meteorological hazard. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A landslide is **both** a **geological hazard** and a **hydro-meteorological hazard**; one label does not explain the other.
xa: Landslides are **associated** with **earthquakes**, **floods** and **volcanic eruptions**.
**Heavy rainfall** is the **main trigger** in India.
Nodal ministry: **Ministry of Mines**.

27.s: In which year was the National Landslide Risk Management Strategy issued?
27.x: The National Landslide Risk Management Strategy was issued in 2019. NDMA's landslide guidelines came in 2009.
27.tq: Discriminate the 2009 guidelines from the 2019 strategy.
n: The National Landslide Risk Management Strategy was issued in 2019. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
xs: The **National Landslide Risk Management Strategy** was issued in **2019** — option **(3)**.
**2009** is the year of the **NDMA Guidelines on Management of Landslides and Snow Avalanches**.
**2024** is the **Wayanad** landslide year.

xa: The **SDRF** is the first responder **within the state** in the first **24–48 hours**.

**Aapda Mitra** trains **community volunteers**.

xa: Prevention, mitigation and preparedness are **pre-disaster** phases.

30.s: In which year was the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act originally enacted?

xs: The **MMDR Act** was enacted in **1957**, so option **(2)** is correct.

xa: **2015** amendment: **auction** mandatory; created the **DMF** and the National Mineral Exploration Trust.

30.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2015 amendment to the MMDR Act?
o: It funded the District Mineral Foundation entirely from the Consolidated Fund of India.

It made auction mandatory for the grant of mineral concessions.

xa: The **DMF** works in **mining-affected districts**.

The **2026** amendment bars States taxing mineral rights except within Central limits.

30.s: Under the 2023 amendment to the MMDR Act, how are critical and strategic minerals such as lithium to be handled?
o: Removed from the scope of mineral legislation
Auctioned by the Centre, with an exploration licence introduced
30.x: The 2023 amendment provided for central auctions of critical and strategic minerals, including lithium, and introduced an exploration licence.

xs: The **2023** amendment has **critical and strategic minerals** (lithium etc.) **auctioned by the Centre**, with an **exploration licence introduced**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Districts and private imports have no such role.
xa: The **2015** amendment made **auction** mandatory and created the **DMF**.
Lithium triangle: **Chile, Argentina, Bolivia**.
AP's **Javakula** gold blocks are under **G2-level** exploration before auction.

30.s: Under the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, how may States tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands?
o: Only within limits prescribed by the Centre
30.x: The 2026 amendment bars States from taxing mineral rights or mineral-bearing lands except within limits prescribed by the Centre.
xa: Passed **14 Aug 2026**.

⚠ **Entry 50** = mineral rights; **Entry 49** = mineral land (State List).

30.s: In Mineral Area Development Authority v. SAIL (2024), the Supreme Court held that States can tax mineral rights under which entry of the State List?
30.x: The nine-judge bench held that States can tax mineral rights under Entry 50 and mineral land under Entry 49, and that royalty is not a tax.
xa: The 2026 Act bars States from taxing mineral rights or mineral-bearing lands except within **Central limits**.
Its **retrospective** clause voids unrecovered State cesses.
**MMDR Act 1957** is the parent law; **2015 amendment** made **auction** mandatory.

30.s: Where in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district did commercial gold mining in Andhra Pradesh begin?
30.x: Commercial gold mining in AP began at Jonnagiri, in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district.
xa: Javakula blocks are under **G2-level** exploration before auction (**29 Jun 2026**).
**Ramagiri** revival includes **reprocessing mine waste**.
World gold region: **Witwatersrand**, South Africa.

30.s: The polymetallic sulphide deposits explored by India on the Carlsberg Ridge are rich in which of the following?
o: Coal, petroleum, natural gas and iron ore
Copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver and gold
30.x: The deposits are rich in copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver and gold; manganese, cobalt, nickel and copper characterise polymetallic nodules.

xs: Carlsberg Ridge sulphides are rich in **copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver and gold**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Manganese, cobalt, nickel, copper** (Mn-Co-Ni-Cu) mark **nodules**, not these sulphides.
xa: India signed the Carlsberg contract in **Sep 2025** with the **ISA**.

o: The Consolidated Fund of the State

30.x: A nine-judge bench held in 2024 that royalty is not a tax.

30.x: ITLOS is in Hamburg; the International Seabed Authority is headquartered in Jamaica.

30.x: Nodules carry manganese, cobalt, nickel and copper; sulphides carry copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver and gold.

30.x: India is rich in coal, iron ore and bauxite and the Himalaya have large hydropower potential; it does not lack fertile land, and the Thar is not a major freshwater source. Moved to resources.

30.s: What is the term for the ratio between the mid diameter and the diameter at breast height?
30.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
30.x: Form quotient is the ratio of the diameter at mid-height (or a fixed height) to the diameter at breast height; form factors are volume ratios. Off-topic (forest mensuration).

30.s: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic used in field identification of timbers?
30.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
30.x: Timbers are identified in the field by physical features such as colour, lustre, hardness, odour, grain and texture; chemical composition needs laboratory analysis, so it is not a field character.

30.s: What is used for manufacturing stainless steel?
30.x: Stainless steel is steel alloyed with chromium and nickel.

30.s: Gems like emerald, ruby and sapphire are compounds of which?
30.x: Ruby and sapphire are corundum (aluminium oxide) and emerald is beryl (beryllium aluminium silicate) – all contain aluminium.

30.s: The precious gem Ruby is mainly aluminium trioxide with trace amount of
30.x: Ruby is corundum (aluminium oxide, Al2O3) coloured red by trace chromium replacing some aluminium ions. Iron and titanium give blue sapphire; manganese, cobalt and silver are not the ruby colourant.

30.s: Main resources of Western Himalayan resource region, are
30.x: The Western Himalayan resource region is a forest (and hydropower) region; metallic, carbonic (coal) and atomic minerals are concentrated in the Peninsular plateau.

30.src: Assistant Director in AP Economics and Statistics 2017
30.x: Tankas (taankas) are the underground rain-water tanks of the Bikaner–Thar region; kuls are Himalayan channels and baolis stepwells.

30.s: Which of the following need not be a characteristic of a "resource"?

30.s: What is the name of traditional rainwater harvesting technique practiced in Thar desert?
30.x: Taanka is the underground tank for harvesting rainwater in the Thar desert (Rajasthan); bawadi is a stepwell and bandhi a bund.

30.s: What produces the blue colour of sapphire?
30.x: Iron and titanium give sapphire (a corundum) its blue colour; chromium gives ruby its red, and chromium or vanadium gives emerald its green.
xa: ⚠ Ruby and sapphire are the **same mineral** (corundum); only the colouring element differs.

30.x: Emerald (beryl) is green due to chromium or vanadium; sapphire is blue due to iron and titanium.

30.x: Emerald is beryl, a beryllium aluminium silicate; ruby and sapphire are corundum.

30.x: The Peninsular plateau is the mineral heartland; the Indo-Gangetic plains are known for alluvium and groundwater, the Himalaya/NE for forests and hydropower, and the Thar for scarce water.

30.x: The Western Ghats are marked by evergreen forests and west-flowing rivers.

30.x: The Himalaya and NE hills are the region of forests, hydropower and jhum lands.

34.tq: Separate the longitudinal-range classification from the regional west-to-east classification.

**Himadri** = Greater, **Himachal** = Lesser, **Shiwalik** = Outer Himalaya.
**Punjab, Kumaon, Nepal** (and Assam) are **regional** divisions; **Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar** are **Trans-Himalayan** ranges.
xa: **Northernmost** of the three = **Himadri**, not the Shiwalik (APPSC-GS 2025).
**Himadri**: loftiest and oldest, average **over 6,000 m**.

xs: The **Indus** rises at **Singge Khabab** — option **(1)**.

The Godavari is 2.7 km wide at Rajahmundry. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 5-10]

37.s: Which of the following is the correct order of rivers from North to South?
37.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
37.x:
Official key: Indus – Ganga – Godavari – Krishna. Strictly, Ganga – Mahanadi – Godavari – Krishna (option 1) is also in north-to-south order.
Indus (Ladakh) – Ganga (northern plains) – Godavari – Krishna runs strictly from north to south, the key. Ganga – Mahanadi – Godavari – Krishna is also north-to-south, so the stem is loose; Yamuna–Ganga and Narmada–Kaveri orders are not clean.

37.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the rivers of India?

A. The main Himalayan river systems are the Ganga, the Indus and the Brahmaputra river systems.

B. The main peninsular river systems include the Narmada, the Tapi, the Godavari, the Krishna, the Kaveri and the Mahanadi river systems.

C. The Indus originates in the northern slopes of the Kailash range in Tibet near Lake Manasarovar.
37.x: All three are true: the Himalayan systems are the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra; the main Peninsular systems are the Narmada, Tapi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri and Mahanadi; and the Indus rises on the northern slopes of the Kailash range near Lake Mansarovar (Bokhar Chu glacier).

37.s: Drainage Pattern of River Krishna is
37.x: Rivers that follow the general slope of the land are consequent rivers; the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, descending from the Western Ghats to the Bay of Bengal, are PMF's examples. Subsequent streams grow along weak rock at right angles; obsequent ones flow against the slope.

37.s: Which of the following rivers divides the Deccan Tableland from Northern India?
37.x: The Narmada flows in a rift valley between the Vindhyas (north) and Satpuras (south), so it separates the Deccan Tableland from northern India. Krishna and Godavari lie wholly within the Peninsula; the Chambal drains the Malwa to the Yamuna.

37.s: Which one of the following east-flowing rivers of India has a rift valley due to down-warping?
37.x: The Damodar flows east through the Chota Nagpur plateau in a rift valley formed by down-warping (a Gondwana trough) and joins the Hugli. Mahanadi, Son and Yamuna do not occupy rift valleys.

37.s: Which of the following rivers is an example of the superimposed river?
37.x: A superimposed river keeps a course formed on an older cover rock and cuts across the structure below; PMF lists the Chambal, Damodar, Subarnarekha and Banas. Alaknanda and Kosi are Himalayan rivers, the Godavari a consequent one.

37.s: Which of the following rivers flows through a rift valley?
37.x:
Most books and keys: Narmada. The Damodar also flows in a rift valley (Gondwana trough), so option 1 is defensible.
The Narmada is the classic rift-valley river, flowing in a fault trough between the Vindhyas and Satpuras. The Damodar's Gondwana trough is also called a rift valley, but the question's intended answer is the Narmada; the Kosi and Godavari are not rift-valley rivers in the textbooks.

37.s: The sequence of the rivers of East Coast from South to North
37.x: From south to north along the east coast the rivers are Cauvery, Pennar, Krishna, Godavari and Mahanadi – the reverse of the UPSC 2002 north-to-south list.

37.s: The correct sequence of the eastward flowing rivers of the peninsular India from north to south is:
o: Subarnarekha, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Pennar, Cauvery and Vaigai
Subarnarekha, Mahanadi, Godavari, Cauvery, Vaigai, Pennar
Mahanadi, Subarnarekha, Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery, Pennar and Vaigai
Mahanadi, Subarnarekha, Krishna, Godavari, Cauvery, Vaigai and Pennar
37.x: North to south the east-flowing Peninsular rivers are Subarnarekha, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Pennar, Cauvery and Vaigai (UPSC 2002 answer a).

37.s: Which of the following rivers flows through rift valley?
37.x: Of the options only the Tapi flows through a rift valley, between the Satpura and Ajanta ranges. Krishna, Mahanadi and Godavari are east-flowing consequent rivers.

37.s: The correct sequence of the eastward flowing rivers of peninsular India from North to South is:
37.x: North to south: Subarnarekha, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Pennar, Cauvery and Vaigai (UPSC 2002, answer a).

37.s: Which of the following rivers passes through a rift valley?
37.x: The Tapi passes through a rift valley between the Satpura and Ajanta ranges, from Multai (Betul, MP) to the Arabian Sea. Krishna, Godavari and Cauvery are not rift-valley rivers.

37.s: Which is the correct arrangement of the following rivers from North to South?
37.x: North to south: Godavari (Maharashtra–AP), Pennar (Rayalaseema–Nellore), Kaveri (Karnataka–TN) and Periyar (central Kerala, the southernmost of the four).

37.s: Which Indian river is called ‘biological desert’?
37.x: The Damodar, flowing through the Chota Nagpur coal and industrial belt, is called a 'biological desert' because heavy industrial effluents have killed much of its aquatic life.

37.s: Which among the following is the correct sequence of rivers starting from North to South?
37.x: By latitude: the Penganga (Vidarbha, ~20°N) lies north of the Godavari, then the Bhima (~17–19°N) and the Tungabhadra (~15°N) in the south.

37.s: Which one of the following rivers flows between Vindhyan and Satpura ranges?
37.x: The Narmada flows between the Vindhyan and Satpura ranges. The Sone, Mahi and Netravati do not.

Consider the following rivers.

II. Ganga

III. Wainganga

37.x: North → south: Kishanganga (Kashmir) – Ganga (northern plains) – Wainganga (rises in Seoni, MP, ~22°N) – Penganga (Buldhana, Maharashtra, ~20°N): I, II, III, IV.

37.s: Unlike Himalayan rivers, through what kind of valleys do Peninsular rivers generally flow?
37.x: Peninsular rivers are usually seasonal and flow in broad, shallow graded valleys, while Himalayan rivers cut deep antecedent gorges.
xa: Mouths: Himalayan rivers form **large deltas**; Peninsular rivers form **deltas (east)** or **estuaries (west)**.
Himalayan rivers are fed by **rain + snowmelt**; Peninsular rivers are **monsoon-fed**.
Use: Himalayan — **irrigation and navigation**; Peninsular — **hydropower**.

37.s: Which drainage pattern, with right-angle bends along joints and faults, is found in the Vindhyan region?
37.x: Rectangular drainage follows joints and faults; the Vindhyan region is the example.

37.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Peninsular rivers?
o: They flow in broad, shallow, graded valleys
They are perennial, fed by snowmelt
37.x: Peninsular rivers are seasonal and monsoon-fed; perennial rain-and-snowmelt regime belongs to Himalayan rivers.

37.s: Which of the following drainage pattern – example pairs is correctly matched?
37.x: Dendritic drainage is seen in the Godavari and Krishna; radial is Amarkantak, centripetal is Loktak.

37.s: The Tapi flows through a rift valley between which ranges?
37.x: The Tapi's rift lies between the Satpura and Ajanta ranges; the Vindhya-Satpura rift belongs to the Narmada.

37.s: Which of these west flowing rivers flows between two mountain ranges?
37.x: The Narmada flows west in a rift valley between two ranges – the Vindhyas in the north and the Satpuras in the south. Sharavati, Mahi and Sabarmati do not flow between two ranges.

37.s: Which is the largest artificial fresh water reservoir in the Country?
37.src: Technical Assistant (Geophysics), Technical Assistants in AP
37.x: The Indira Sagar dam on the Narmada (Khandwa, MP) holds the largest reservoir in India by volume of water stored; Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna is second. Gandhi Sagar (Chambal) and Shivaji Sagar (Koyna) are smaller.

37.s: Which of the following river originate in M.P. and drops its water into the Gulf of Khambhat?
37.x: The Mahi rises in the Vindhyas (Dhar, MP), flows through Banswara in Rajasthan and Gujarat and enters the Gulf of Khambhat. The Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch; the Parvati and Jawai are tributaries of the Chambal and Luni.

37.s: Which of the following rivers falls into the Arabian Sea?
37.x: The Tapti rises at Multai (Betul, MP) and drains into the Arabian Sea at Suvali near Surat. The Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi empty into the Bay of Bengal.

37.s: Which of the following rivers does not falls into the Bay of Bengal?
37.x: The Tapti flows west to the Arabian Sea, so it does not fall into the Bay of Bengal. The Mahanadi, Krishna and Godavari all reach the Bay of Bengal.

37.s: Which of the following rivers fall into the Arabian sea?
37.x: The Tapi is west-flowing and drains into the Arabian Sea at Suvali near Surat. The Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi flow into the Bay of Bengal.

37.s: Which river has as many as 29 dams constructed on it?
37.x:
Printed key: Mahanadi. The verified '29' is the Narmada: 29 major projects in MP of the 30 major dams planned (NVDA).
The Narmada Valley plan has 30 major dams; the Madhya Pradesh government planned 29 major projects on the Narmada (plus Sardar Sarovar in Gujarat), which is where the '29 dams' figure comes from. No source supports 29 dams on the Mahanadi.

37.s: Which of the following is not a tributary of the river Narmada?

37.x: Aliabet, Sarfuddin, Dashan, Mehgam and Vegni are riverine islands of the Narmada estuary.

37.x: The Cheruthoni dam (part of the Idukki project) is on the Cheruthoni, a tributary of the Periyar in Idukki, Kerala.

37.x: The Tawa is the longest tributary of the Narmada; it rises in the Mahadeo hills and joins at Bandra Bhan (Narmadapuram).

37.s: Mithi river of Mumbai originates from which of the following lakes ?
37.x: The Mithi rises at Vihar Lake in Mumbai; Powai Lake water joins it and it falls into Mahim Bay.

37.s: Which of the following districts is a part of Narmada basin?
37.x: The Narmada basin covers a small part of Chhattisgarh on the Maikal slopes (Kabirdham/Rajnandgaon area). Raipur and Korba lie in the Mahanadi basin and Bastar in the Godavari (Indravati) basin.

37.s: Purna river is a tributary of which of the following rivers?
37.x: The Purna is one of the largest (left-bank) tributaries of the Tapi.

37.s: Tawa Project is associated with which state?
37.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
37.x: The Tawa project is on the Tawa, the Narmada's longest tributary, near Itarsi (Narmadapuram/Hoshangabad), Madhya Pradesh.

37.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud

37.x: The Tapi (724 km) is the second longest west-flowing river after the Narmada (1,312 km).

37.x: The Tawa is the longest Narmada tributary; it joins at Bandra Bhan, Narmadapuram.

37.x: Sabarmati is associated with Ahmedabad, whereas Surat is associated with the Tapi. Mithi, Mula-Mutha and Musi are correctly matched with Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad respectively.

37.x: Ahmedabad is on the Sabarmati. Kota is on the Chambal, Gorakhpur on the Rapti and Pandharpur on the Chandrabhaga.

Kota is situated on Chambal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]

37.s: Within India, Ganga river basin has the largest catchment area. After that, following is the correct sequence in the decreasing order:

The app's old notes record the APPSC (2024) key as Brahmaputra > Indus > Godavari > Krishna (not verified here). By basin area within India: Indus > Godavari > Krishna > Brahmaputra.
Within India the basin areas are Ganga (~8.6 lakh sq km) > Indus (3,21,289) > Godavari (3,12,812) > Krishna (2,58,948) > Brahmaputra (~1.94 lakh), so the order after the Ganga is Indus > Godavari > Krishna > Brahmaputra.

37.s: Which one of the following river basins is the largest in respect to area?

37.s: The longest peninsular river of India is -

37.x: The order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (about 1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (851 km) and Tapi (724 km).

37.x: The Narmada (1,312 km) is the longest west-flowing river; the Tapi (724 km) is second.

37.s: Which two peninsular river basins are about the same size?
37.x: The Narmada (98,796 sq km) and Kaveri (81,155 sq km) basins are about the same size.

37.s: With reference to the river Luni, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It flows into the Gulf of Khambhat.
It flows into the Gulf of Kuchchh.
It flows into Pakistan and merges with a tributary of the Indus.

37.s: In which of the following rivers, the upper course contains freshwater but saline water flowing at the lower part?
37.x: The Luni's water is fresh in its upper course but becomes saline lower down as it crosses the salt-bearing desert, before being lost in the Rann of Kutch. The Barak and Ghaggar do not show this.

37.s: Which of the following is a land-bounded river ?
37.x: The Luni is land-bound (endorheic): it is lost in the Rann of Kutch and never reaches the sea. The Tapti, Krishna and Narmada flow into the sea.

37.s: Which one of the following statements is not true?
o: Ghaggar's water is utilized in the Indira Gandhi Canal
Nizam Sagar is situated on the Manjra river
Penganga is a tributary of the Godavari
37.x: Statement (a) is false: the Indira Gandhi Canal is fed from the Harike barrage on the Sutlej–Beas, not by the Ghaggar. The Narmada does rise at Amarkantak, Nizam Sagar is on the Manjira and the Penganga is a Godavari tributary.

37.s: Which of the following river has Internal Drainage System?

37.x: The Luni has internal (inland, endorheic) drainage – it is lost in the Rann of Kutch. The Narmada, Penna and Tapti reach the sea.

38.s: According to the classical thermal theory of the monsoon, the summer monsoon is produced primarily because:
o: The ITCZ remains fixed south of the equator throughout the year.

38.tq: Apply the pressure-gradient logic of differential heating rather than memorising only the theory’s name.
xs: **Land heats faster than sea**, creating a **summer low over land** that draws moist sea winds — option **(2)**.

38.s: The dynamic or ITCZ theory explains the southwest monsoon mainly through:

The southward shift of the ITCZ over the Indian Ocean during summer.
The permanent eastward movement of the subtropical westerly jet over peninsular India.
38.x: In summer, the ITCZ shifts northward over the Ganga plain as the monsoon trough. South-east trades cross the equator and are deflected to become south-westerly winds.

A **southward** ITCZ shift is the opposite of the summer pattern.
xa: During **breaks**, the trough shifts to the **Himalayan foothills**.
**STJ** north of the Himalayas → **onset**; back south → **withdrawal**.
Thermal theory: Sir Edmund **Halley**, **1686**.

2. Statement-II: The high temperature and moisture of tropical rain forests cause dead organic matter in the soil to decompose quickly. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

43.x: Soils in tropical rainforests are generally poor in nutrients. Intense and continuous rainfall leads to leaching, where soluble nutrients are washed away from the topsoil, preventing their accumulation. The high temperature and humidity in tropical rainforests accelerate the decomposition of organic matter. Microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi rapidly break down dead plants and animals, releasing nutrients. Although nutrients are released quickly, they are immediately absorbed by dense vegetation or lost through leaching. As a result, the soil itself does not become nutrient-rich.

Laterite Soil *F.Buchanan- Hamilton carried out research on Laterite soil for the first time in 1807. Its name has been derived from the Latin word ‘Later’ which means ‘brick’. *These soils are as soft as butter when wet but become harder like bricks when dry. Map Not to Scale *The laterite soil is formed under conditions of high temperature and heavy rainfall with alternate wet and dry periods, which leads to the leaching of soil, leaving only oxides of iron and aluminium. 43.s: In India, the largest soil group is found as :
43.x: Alluvial soil is the largest and most important soil group in India. Covering about 15 lakh sq. km or about 45.6% of the total land area of the country, these soils contribute the largest share of our agricultural wealth. The widest occurrence of the Alluvial soils is in the Indo-Gangetic plain starting from Punjab in the West to West Bengal and Assam in the East. They are also found in deltas of Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery, where they are called deltaic alluvium. Along the coast, they are known as coastal alluvium. Some alluvial soils are found in Narmada and Tapi (Tapti) valleys. Geologically, the alluvium is divided into newer or younger Khadar and older Bhangar soils. 43.x: The parent rock of black cotton soil is fissure volcanic rock, which consists of igneous rocks formed from the cooling and solidification of lava that erupted through fissures (cracks) in the Earth's crust. These soils are black in colour and are also known as regur soils. Black soil is ideal for growing cotton and is also known as black cotton soil. This type of soil is typical of the Deccan trap (Basalt) region, which spans the northwest Deccan plateau and consists of lava flows. 43.x: Conservation agriculture is a method that keep agricultural cost low. High profits and sustainable product can be brought. Along with this, there is a balanced increase in natural resources like soil, water, environment, and biological factors. In this, there is a balanced and proper use of agricultural chemicals and inorganic and organic sources along with agricultural activities such as zero tillage/minimum tillage, so that there is no adverse effect on the various bio-functions of agriculture. In conservation agriculture, minimum tillage allows crop residues to remain on the soil surface. This greatly reduces soil erosion. Generally it is very important to keep the soil covered by crop residues up to 30 percent. It is very important to adopt crop diversification and crop rotation in protected cultivation.Generally, farmers follow the same type of crop rotation for many years. For example, farmers have been planting the paddy wheat cropping system in the same field for years, which directly affected the fertility of the soil. It does impact crop diversification maintains soil fertility and reduces crop related pests and diseases.

44.x: Statement I is incorrect: Section 15 of the MMDR Act empowers the State Governments to make rules for regulating the grant of quarry leases, mining leases or other mineral concessions in respect of minor minerals and for purposes connected therewith. 44.x: Bentonite is incorrect: A mineral is a naturally occurring substance characterized by unique chemical and physical properties, composition, and atomic structure. In India, minerals are classified as major or minor under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2015, to assess output value in the mining and quarrying sector. As per Government of India official notification released in 2015 Bentonite (locally known as multani mitti or Fuller's earth) has been declared as 'Minor Mineral'. Chromite is correct: Chromite is a major mineral. It is a dark grey, metallic, oxide mineral often mistaken for magnetite due to its metallic lustre and occasional magnetic properties. It can be found in basic igneous rocks, as well as in metamorphic and sedimentary rocks formed from weather-affected chromite-bearing rocks. It is a crucial metal used to make hard, tough, and chemically resistant steel. The chromium extracted from chromite is used in chrome plating and alloying to produce corrosion-resistant superalloys, nichrome, and stainless steel. More than 96% of chromite resources are located in Odisha (Jajpur, Kendujhar, and Dhenkanal). Kyanite is correct: Kyanite is a major mineral. It occurs in metamorphic aluminous rocks. It has high-temperature resilience. Its quality relies on aluminium content: more aluminium, higher grade. It is primarily used in metallurgical, ceramic, glass, and cement industries. It is also used to make spark plugs in automobiles. Jhark

Renowned as the ‘Blue Mountains’, Nilgiri Hills are located at the junction of Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats. Doddabetta is the highest peak in the Nilgiri Hills at 2,637 metres. The Anaimalai or Anamalai Hills form the southern portion of the Western Ghats and span up to the border of Kerala and Tamil Nadu in southern India. 48.s: Telugu Ganga Canal Water is supplied to which of the following states?
48.x:
The Telugu Ganga Project is an inter-state water project designed primarily to supply drinking water to Chennai (Tamil Nadu) while also providing irrigation benefits to Andhra Pradesh. The project utilizes surplus waters of the Krishna River and conveys them through a network of reservoirs and canals. Water flows through Srisailam Reservoir, Somasila Reservoir, Kandaleru Reservoir, and finally reaches Poondi Reservoir near Chennai. Apart from supplying drinking water to Chennai, the project also provides irrigation facilities to drought-prone districts of Rayalaseema and parts of Nellore district. The project is an example of interstate cooperation involving Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. However, the state receiving drinking water under the project is Tamil Nadu. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Purpose – Drinking water supply to Chennai
• Beneficiary State – Tamil Nadu
• Major Reservoirs – Srisailam, Somasila, Kandaleru

The Godavari basin extends over Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha, as well as smaller parts of Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Puducherry. The Godavari basin is the second-largest basin in India.The River rises from Trimbakeshwar in the Nashik district of Maharashtra. It is the largest peninsular Indian river that drains into the Bay of Bengal. It divides into two main streams, the Gautami Godavari on the east and the Vashishta Godavari on the west and forms a large delta before it pours into the Bay of Bengal. The delta of the Godavari is lobate, with a rounded bulge and numerous distributaries. • Important cities: Nashik, Paithan, Nizamabad, Rajahmundry, etc., • Right bank tributaries: Pravara, Manjira, and Maner. • Left bank tributaries: Purna, Pranahita, Indravathi, and Sabari Indian Geography PMF IAS Geo – 83 • Indravati River: It flows through the states of Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh in India. It originates in the Eastern Ghats in the Kalahandi district of Odisha and flows for a distance of 535 kilometres before joining the Godavari River at Bhadrachalam in Telangana. • Pranahita: It flows through the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh in India. It joins the Godavari River at Khammam in Telangana. Vamsadhara is incorrect: The Vamsadhara River flows through the states of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. 51.s: The Nallamala Hills extend through which region of Andhra Pradesh?
51.x: Nallamala extends through Nandyal, Prakasam and Palnadu; Seshachalam is in Tirupati–Annamayya and Palakonda in Kadapa–Annamayya.

The **K-G mouths** (Kakinada, Krishna, Bapatla) carry **"Koringa forests"**.

51.s: Jerdon's courser is protected in which wildlife sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh?
51.x: Jerdon's courser, a critically endangered nocturnal bird, is protected in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2024** match: **Coringa-saltwater crocodile**, **Rollapadu-GIB**, **Sri Lankamalleswara-Jerdon's courser**.

51.s: Which is the smallest wildlife sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh?
51.x: Nelapattu (4.58 sq km) is the smallest sanctuary; Rollapadu is 6.14 sq km.
xa: Largest PA: **NSTR/Rajiv Gandhi WLS**.
Rajiv Gandhi NP was notified in **2005**.
Nelapattu (**Tirupati**) is a **pelican breeding** site.

51.s: In which district is Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary located?
51.x: Sri Lankamalleswara sanctuary is in Kadapa (Cuddapah); Nelapattu is in Tirupati district.
n: Sri Lanka Malleshwara Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Cuddapah. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Nelapattu Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Tirupathi district. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
xa: Sri Lankamalleswara (**464.42 sq km**) is the home of **Jerdon's Courser**; notified **1988**.
Nelapattu (**4.58 sq km**) is the **smallest** sanctuary — a **pelican breeding** site.
**Pulicat WLS** is also in **Tirupathi** — known for **flamingos**.
**Sri Venkateswara WLS** is in **Annamayya, Tirupati**.

51.s: Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which districts?
51.x: Krishna WLS lies in Bapatla and Krishna districts and protects the Krishna estuary mangroves.
xa: Krishna WLS area: **194.81 sq km**.
Older notes list Krishna WLS as "**Machilipatnam**"; use the **2024-25** districts.
Mangroves grow mainly in the **Godavari and Krishna estuaries**.

51.s: Inside which protected area does Sri Venkateswara National Park lie?
51.x: Sri Venkateswara NP lies inside Sri Venkateswara WLS in the Seshachalam and Tirumala hills.
xa: SV NP notified **1989**; areas WLS **172.34** / NP **353.63 sq km**.
SV NP flagships: **Indian leopard**, **Indian giant squirrel**, golden gecko.
**Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve** (**2010**) is AP's only BR.

51.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuary — Kadapa and Nellore — Penusila hills
Papikonda National Park — Eluru and Alluri Sitharama Raju — Godavari gorge
Kambalakonda Wildlife Sanctuary — Visakhapatnam — Eastern Ghats near Vizag
Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary — Chittoor — borders Tamil Nadu
51.x: Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuary is in Annamayya and Tirupati districts and is associated with the Seshachalam and Tirumala hills. Kadapa and Nellore with the Penusila hills refers to Sri Penusila Narasimha Wildlife Sanctuary.
51.tq: Look for the swapped sanctuary–district–landscape association.
xs: **Sri Venkateswara WLS — Kadapa and Nellore — Penusila hills** is wrongly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
SV WLS is in **Annamayya, Tirupati** (**Seshachalam**, Tirumala hills); Kadapa-Nellore + **Penusila hills** = **Sri Penusila Narasimha WLS**.
The others are right: **Papikonda NP** (Eluru, ASR, Godavari gorge); **Kambalakonda** (Visakhapatnam); **Koundinya** (Chittoor, borders TN).
xa: SV WLS / NP areas: **172.34 / 353.63 sq km**; the NP lies **inside** the SV WLS; NP notified **1989**.
Penusila Narasimha area: **1,030.86 sq km** (**404.43 + 626.43**).
Kambalakonda area: **70.70 sq km**.

51.s: Which protected area is described as the only elephant habitat in Andhra Pradesh?
51.x: Kaundinya Wildlife Sanctuary is associated with the Asian elephant and is described as the only elephant habitat in Andhra Pradesh.
51.tq: Identify the protected area from the exclusive habitat description.
xs: **Kaundinya WLS** is AP's **only elephant habitat** (**Asian elephant**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Gundla Brahmeswaram** is a **tiger corridor**; **SV** has the **Indian leopard**; **Papikonda** has **tiger, gaur, mouse deer**.
xa: Kaundinya: **Chittoor**, **357.60 sq km**, borders **Tamil Nadu**; notified **1990**.
Elephant reserve = **Koundinya + Rayala Elephant Reserve**.
Man-animal conflict compensation: **Rs 130 lakh** paid up to **Dec 2025**.

51.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kaundinya Wildlife Sanctuary — Great Indian Bustard

51.tq: Start from the sure species–sanctuary pair and eliminate the swapped associations.
xs: **Coringa WLS — saltwater crocodile** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Rollapadu** → **Great Indian Bustard**; **Kaundinya** → **Asian elephant**; **Kolleru** → migratory water birds; **Jerdon's courser** → **Sri Lankamalleswara**.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2024** match: **Coringa-saltwater crocodile**, **Rollapadu-GIB**, **Sri Lankamalleswara-Jerdon's courser**.
**Indian leopard** is a **Sri Venkateswara NP** flagship.
**Papikonda NP**: tiger, gaur, mouse deer, **kanchu mekha**.

51.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Koringa Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Kakinada.
Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Nellore district.
Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Tirupathi district.
Rajiv Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Kurnool and Prakasam.
51.x: Option B is incorrect: Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary is in Chittoor, not Nellore. Koringa in Kakinada, Sri Venkateswara in Tirupati and Rajiv Gandhi in Kurnool–Prakasam are right.
51.tq: Check the district in each statement.
n: Koringa Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Kakinada. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Chittoor. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Tirupathi. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Rajiv Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary, a tiger reserve, is located in Kurnool and Prakasam. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Kakinada. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Nellore district**" — option **(2)**.
**Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary** is in **Chittoor**.
**Koringa** is in **Kakinada**, **Sri Venkateswara** in **Tirupathi**, **Rajiv Gandhi** in **Kurnool and Prakasam** — all correct.
xa: Koundinya (**357.60 sq km**) borders Tamil Nadu — AP's only **Asian elephant** habitat.
Koundinya was notified in **1990**.
Elephants moved into **Palamaner/Kaundinya** in the **1980s** due to drought in **Hosur-Dharmapuri** and **Bannerghatta**.
AP has **13 wildlife sanctuaries, 3 national parks**.

51.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?

n: Kolleru Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Eluru. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Machilipatnam. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Kurnool district. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Gundla Brahmeswara Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Kurnool district. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
xa: **Kolleru** became a **Ramsar site in 2002**; breeding ground of the **spot-billed pelican**.
Rollapadu (**6.14 sq km**) also has **blackbuck** and **wolf**.

51.s: Gundla Brahmeswaram Wildlife Sanctuary is characterised by which of the following?
o: Pelican breeding colony and migratory waterfowl
Dry deciduous forest and the new CR herb Euphorbia chalamensis
51.x: Gundla Brahmeswaram (Nandyal-Prakasam, the extended core of NSTR in the Nallamala) is a dry deciduous forest sanctuary where the new Critically Endangered (CR) herb Euphorbia chalamensis was recorded in 2026. Pelican colonies (Nelapattu), brackish lagoon flamingos (Pulicat) and mangrove crocodiles (Coringa) belong to other sanctuaries.
51.tq: Identify the habitat-feature pair rather than the better-known wetland associations.
xs: **Gundla Brahmeswaram WLS** has **dry deciduous forest** and the new CR herb **Euphorbia chalamensis** (**2026**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Pelican colony** = **Nelapattu**; **brackish lagoon + flamingos** = **Pulicat**; **mangroves + saltwater crocodile** = **Coringa**.
xa: It is the **NSTR extended core** in the **Nallamala** (**Nandyal, Prakasam**).
It acts as a **tiger corridor** next to NSTR.

51.s: Which is Andhra Pradesh's only biosphere reserve, notified in 2010?
51.x: The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve (4,755.997 sq km, 2010) is AP's only biosphere reserve. Some sources wrongly call it the Sri Venkateswara BR; SV is a national park and sanctuary. Nallamala holds the NSTR tiger reserve and Papikonda is a national park.
xs: AP's only BR, notified **2010**, is the **Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Some notes wrongly call it the **Sri Venkateswara** BR; SV is a **NP and WLS**. Nallamala holds **NSTR**; Papikonda is an **NP**.
xa: Area: **4,755.997 sq km**; spread over the **Tirupati and Kurnool circles**.
**Red Sanders** is endemic to the **Seshachalam**, Palakonda and Veligonda ranges.
Survey count: **1 tiger reserve and 1 biosphere reserve**.

51.s: In which year was Kolleru Lake, a freshwater lake between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, designated a Ramsar site?
51.x: Kolleru was declared a Ramsar site in 2002. 1999 is the year Kolleru was notified as a wildlife sanctuary, 2008 is when Papikonda became a national park, and 2010 is when the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve was notified.
xs: **Kolleru** became a **Ramsar site in 2002** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**1999** = Kolleru notified as WLS; **2008** = Papikonda NP; **2010** = Seshachalam BR.
xa: Kolleru WLS: **308.55 sq km**, **Eluru / West Godavari**.
It is a **freshwater lake** between the **Krishna and Godavari** deltas.
Flagship: **spot-billed pelican** and migratory water birds.

51.s: The Rajiv Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary, which is a tiger reserve and part of the Nallamala landscape, extends over which districts according to APSES 2024–25?
o: Eluru, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Kakinada
51.x: The Rajiv Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary (Tiger Reserve) extends over Nandyal, Prakasam and Palnadu districts and forms part of the Nallamala landscape.

xs: **Rajiv Gandhi WLS (Tiger Reserve)** spans **Nandyal, Prakasam and Palnadu** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is in the **Nallamala** and forms the **core of NSTR**.
xa: Largest PA: **NSTR/Rajiv Gandhi WLS**.
**Rajiv Gandhi NP** (**2.30 sq km**) is AP's smallest NP, notified **2005**.

51.s: With which area are dry deciduous forests mainly associated in Andhra Pradesh?
51.x: Dry deciduous forests cover the Seshachalam–Nallamala belt, and the forest region reaches south to the Palakonda and Nallamala hills.
n: Dry deciduous forests are associated with the Seshachalam–Nallamala belt. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 41-43]
The southern extent of the forest region reaches the Palakonda and Nallamala Hills. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 41-43]
xa: **Northern** extent: **Simhachalam Hills**; **western**: **Balaghat Hills**.
**Palakonda hills** (Kadapa-Annamayya): dry deciduous; **Red Sanders** belt.
**Nallamala** = largest forest in AP; home of **NSTR**.

51.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nallamala Hills — dry deciduous forests and Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve
Seshachalam Hills — tidal mangrove forests and Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary
Palakonda Hills — moist evergreen forests and Papikonda National Park
Krishna-Godavari mouths — thorn forests and Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary
51.x: The Nallamala Hills are characterised by dry deciduous forests and include the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve. The other pairs incorrectly assign forest types or protected areas.
51.tq: Start with the sure region–forest-type association and eliminate swapped locations.
xs: **Nallamala Hills — dry deciduous forests and NSTR** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Seshachalam** is **dry deciduous** with **Red Sanders**; **Coringa** mangroves are at the **Krishna-Godavari mouths**.
**Palakonda** is dry deciduous (Red Sanders belt); the K-G mouths are **tidal / mangrove**, while **Rollapadu** is grassland.
xa: Nallamala = **largest forest** in AP (**Nandyal-Prakasam-Palnadu**).
Rainfall types: moist/tidal **125-200 cm**; dry deciduous **75-100 cm**.
Forest-bearing hills: North **Simhachalam**; West **Balaghat**; South **Palakonda and Nallamala**.

51.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of protected areas located in Telangana?

Nagarhole, Mrugavani and Coringa Wildlife Sanctuaries
51.x: Mrugavani National Park, Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park and Eturunagaram Wildlife Sanctuary are located in Telangana.

xs: **Mrugavani, Kasu Brahmananda Reddy NP and Eturunagaram WLS** are all in **Telangana** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Papikonda**, **Coringa, Krishna, Rollapadu** are AP areas; **Nagarhole** is in **Karnataka**.

52.s: A fertile soil, suitable for growing common crops is likely to have a pH value of :
52.x: The soil pH is a measure of the acidity or alkalinity in soils. A pH below 7 is acidic and above 7 is alkaline. Soil pH is considered a master variable in soils as it controls many chemical processes that take place. It specifically affects plant nutrient availability by controlling the chemical forms of the nutrients. Most nutrients that plants need can dissolve easily when the pH of the soil solution ranges from 6.0 to 7.0. Thus, option (c) is correct.

Rainfall *Generally in India rainfall occurs from the month of June to September when south-west monsoon is effective throughout the country. In this period, the low-pressure zone of North- Western India is very intense and systematic. Due to low air pressure, south-east winds from the tropic of Capricorn in the Southern Hemisphere cross the equator and are attracted towards the Indian Peninsula. Passing over the oceans these winds are filled with humidity and split into two branches - Arabian Sea branch and Bay of Bengal branch. *When the south-west monsoon winds enter the terrestrial area, it rains with an intense thundering and torrential storms. The arrival of these winds and rainfall is called ‘burst’ of the monsoon. *The speed of these winds is about 30 km/h on average and they become effective throughout the country within a month. *According to the data Rainfall Statistics of India (2024), almost the entire rainfall is received from the southwest monsoon (June-September). *Monsoon winds of the Arabian Sea are obstructed by the Western Ghats. These winds climb the slope of the Western Ghats and soon become cool causing heavy rainfall on the windward side of Western Ghats. These winds cause little rainfall to the east of the Western Ghats. The region of low rainfall is known as the rain-shadow area

In Italy, the average number of children per woman fell from 1.24 in 2022 to 1.2 in 2023, as per government data. Experts warn that if the current demographic trend persists, Italy's population — currently around 59 million — could shrink by nearly 1 million by 2030. In South Korea, government figures indicate an 8% drop in the fertility rate in 2023 compared to the previous year. (South Korea's birthrate rose in 2024 for the first time in nine years). Additional Information: What is the 'fertility rate' and how different it's from 'birth rate'? Both fertility rate and birth rate are indicators of population growth, but they are not the same. The fertility rate indicates the average number of children a woman of childbearing age is expected to have; a fertility rate of 2.1 is considered the "replacement rate." On the other hand, the birth rate measures the number of live births per 1,000 people in a given population each year. More dependants raise the dependency ratio, working against the dividend.

66.s: Which of the following criteria is not used for the classification of human races?
66.x: Racial classification uses skin, eye and hair colour/form, plus cephalic, nasal and stature indices and blood groups. Ear is not among these criteria, so it is the answer.

66.s: Which racial group has the largest number of members?
66.x: The notes do not give the population sizes of the racial groups. Caucasoid is the largest group worldwide.

66.s: Which of the following correctly represents the cephalic index?
o: Maximum length divided by maximum breadth, multiplied by 100
Maximum breadth divided by maximum length, multiplied by 100
Stature divided by head length, multiplied by 100
Nasal breadth divided by nasal length, multiplied by 100
66.x: Cephalic index is calculated as (maximum breadth / maximum length) × 100.
66.tq: Recall the exact formula rather than the reversed ratio.
xs: **Cephalic index = (maximum breadth / maximum length) x 100** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) inverts the ratio; stature and nasal measures are separate indices.
xa: **Brachycephalic** (round) = living head CI **82 and above**.
**Dolichocephalic** (long) = living head CI **76.99** and below.
**S.S. Sarkar** built his **six ethnic elements** on the cephalic index.

66.s: A person has a nasal index of 86. Under the stated classification, this person would belong to which nasal category?
66.x: Platyrrhine refers to a broad nose with a nasal index of 85 or above. Leptorrhine is below 70 and mesorrhine is 70–84.9.
66.tq: Apply the numerical boundary to the category instead of recalling labels alone.
xs: A nasal index of **86** is **Platyrrhine** (broad nose; **85 and above**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mesorrhine** = **70-84.9**; **Leptorrhine** = under **70**.
**Dolichocephalic** is a head-shape term, not a nasal one.
xa: **Risley** ranked castes mainly by the **nasal index**.
Risley's dictum: caste status varies **inversely** with nasal index.
⚠ **Risley** = nasal index; **Sarkar** = cephalic index; **Haddon** = hair form.

66.s: The cephalic index of a living person is 83. What is this head type under the standard classification?
66.x: For a living head, a cephalic index of 82 and above is brachycephalic (round-headed), 77-81.99 is mesocephalic and 76.99 and below is dolichocephalic (long-headed), so 83 is brachycephalic. Platyrrhine is a nasal-index class (85 and above), not a head type.
66.tq: Living head CI: ≤76.99 dolicho, 77-81.99 meso, ≥82 brachy.
xs: A living CI of **83** is **Brachycephalic** (round; **82 and above**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Mesocephalic** = **77-81.99**; **Dolichocephalic** = **76.99** and below.
**Platyrrhine** is a nasal category.
xa: Dry skull: brachycephalic = **80 and above**.
Guha's **Western Brachycephals**: Alpinoid, Dinaric, Armenoid.
CI = (maximum breadth / maximum length) x **100**.

66.s: Which racial group is associated with straight, coarse hair described as leiotrichi?
66.x: Straight, coarse hair, termed leiotrichi, is associated with the Mongoloid group. Woolly or frizzy hair, termed ulotrichi, is associated with the Negroid group.
66.tq: Distinguish the similar hair classifications by their exact technical terms.
xs: **Leiotrichi** (straight, coarse hair) is **Mongoloid** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Cymotrichi** (straight-wavy) = **Caucasoid**; **ulotrichi** (woolly) = **Negroid**.
xa: ⚠ **leio – cymo – ulo** = **straight – wavy – woolly**.
**Haddon (1924)** used **hair form** as the main basis for world populations.
Mongoloids have **sparse hair**.

66.s: Which of the following descriptions of racial groups is INCORRECT?
o: Mongoloids – light skin, wavy hair, narrow noses, tall stature
Caucasoids – light to olive skin, straight or wavy hair, narrow noses
Mongoloids – straight black hair, epicanthic folds, broad faces
Negroids – dark skin, woolly hair, broad noses, thick lips
66.x: Option 1 is the incorrect description: wavy hair and a narrow nose are Caucasoid traits, while Mongoloids have straight hair, oblique eyes with an epicanthic fold and a flat face. The Caucasoid and Negroid (woolly hair, broad nose) descriptions are correct.
n: Caucasoids have light to olive skin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids have straight or wavy hair. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids have narrow noses. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids have yellowish to brown skin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids have straight black hair. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids have an epicanthic fold. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids have broad faces. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids have dark brown to black skin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids have woolly or curly hair. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids have broad noses. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids have thick lips. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]

66.s: How is a height of 170 cm and above classified on Topinard's stature scale?
66.x: Topinard's scale puts 170 cm and above as tall and under 160 cm as small.
