66.s: A cephalic index of 76.99 and below (living person) indicates which head type?
66.x: 76.99 and below is dolichocephalic (long head); 82+ is brachycephalic.
66.tq: one-liner

66.s: In racial classification by hair form, which group has woolly hair, described as ulotrichi?
66.x: Ulotrichi (woolly) hair marks the Negroid group; leiotrichi is straight (Mongoloid) and cymotrichi is wavy (Caucasoid).

66.s: The Caucasoid racial group is mainly distributed across which of the following regions?
o: East Asia, Southeast Asia, Central Asia, and Arctic regions
Most populations of West, Central and Southern Africa
Australia, Australian Melanesia and Sub-Saharan Africa
Europe, North Africa, Middle East, and parts of Central and South Asia
66.x: Caucasoids are spread across Europe, North Africa, the Middle East and parts of Central and South Asia.
66.tq: Recall the region of each racial group.
n: Caucasoids are distributed in Europe. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids are distributed in North Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids are distributed in the Middle East. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids are distributed in parts of Central Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids are distributed in parts of South Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids are distributed in East Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids are distributed in Southeast Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids are distributed in Central Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids are found in the Arctic. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids are distributed among most populations of West Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids are distributed among most populations of Central Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids are distributed among most populations of Southern Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids are associated with Sub-Saharan Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Australoids are distributed in Australia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Australoids are distributed in Australian Melanesia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
xs: Caucasoids are spread across **Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, and parts of Central and South Asia** — option **(4)**.
**East Asia, Southeast Asia, Central Asia and the Arctic** is the **Mongoloid** range.
**West, Central and Southern Africa** is the **Negroid** range; **Australia** and **Australian Melanesia** are **Australoid**.
xa: Caucasoid traits: **light to olive skin**, **straight or wavy hair**, **narrow noses**, medium to tall stature.
Caucasoids include **Europeans, Arabs, Persians, many North Indians**.
Caucasoid hair is **cymotrichi** (straight-wavy); blood group **more A than B**.

66.s: Which racial type is described by a long head, depressed nasal root and wavy hair?
66.x: The Proto-Australoid type is described by a long head, depressed nasal root and wavy hair.
66.tq: Identify the classification from its distinguishing physical traits.
xs: A **long head**, **depressed nasal root** and **wavy hair** mark the **Proto-Australoid** — option **(4)** is correct.
Proto-Australoids also have **dark skin**, a **broad flat nose** and short-to-medium stature.
**Negrito** have **woolly/frizzy** hair; **Nordic** are tall and fair; **Western Brachycephals** are broad-headed.
xa: Guha's Proto-Australoids: **Santhal, Munda, Oraon, Ho, Bhil, Chenchu** (central and southern India).
**Santhal** = standard central-India example (UPPSC **2002** key).
AP's **Chenchus** (Nallamala) = Proto-Australoid.

66.s: The description ‘yellow complexion, oblique eyes, high cheek bones, sparse hair and medium height’ refers to which racial type?
66.x: Yellow complexion, oblique eyes, high cheek bones, sparse hair and medium height are characteristic descriptions associated with the Mongoloid type.
66.tq: Discriminate between racial types by their distinctive physical descriptions.
xs: **Yellowish complexion, oblique eyes, high cheekbones, sparse hair, medium height** describe the **Mongoloid** — option **(3)** is correct (UPSC **1997** key).
Mongoloids also have a **broad head** and **flat face**.
**Negrito** have dark skin and woolly hair; **Nordic** are tall and fair.
xa: Mongoloid eye: **medial epicanthic fold**; hair **leiotrichi** (straight, coarse); blood group **high B**.
**North-east** tribes = Mongoloid (UPPSC **2003** key).
**Shompen** of Great Nicobar are Mongoloid.

66.s: A high nasal bridge and a narrow nose are characteristic of which racial group?
66.x: Caucasoids have a high bridge and narrow nose; Mongoloids a low-to-medium bridge; Negroids a low bridge and broad nose.
xa: Skin: Caucasoid pale reddish-white to olive brown; Mongoloid **saffron to yellow-brown**; Negroid brown to brown-black.
⚠ **leio – cymo – ulo** = **straight – wavy – woolly**.

66.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
66.x: Pygmies live in the Congo Basin; Inuit in the Arctic, Native Americans in the Americas and Negritos in the Andamans and South-east Asia.
n: Pygmies are found in the Congo Basin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Pygmies are found in Central Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Pygmies have short stature. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Eskimos are also called Inuit. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Eskimos or Inuit are found in Arctic regions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Eskimos or Inuit are classified as Mongoloids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Native Americans are found in the Americas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Native Americans have Mongoloid origin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negritos are found in the Andaman Islands. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negritos are found in parts of Southeast Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negritos are found in parts of India. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negritos have short stature. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negritos have dark skin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negritos have woolly hair. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids include Native Americans. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Eskimos are included among Mongoloids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
xa: Pygmy stature: **1.3–1.5 metres**.
Andaman Negritos: **Onge, Jarawa, Great Andamanese, Sentinelese**.
The **Shompen** of Nicobar are **Mongoloid**, unlike the Andaman Negritos.

66.s: Aboriginal Australians and some Melanesians are associated with which racial group?
66.x: The Australoid group includes Aboriginal Australians and some Melanesians.
n: Australoids are associated with Aboriginals. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Australoids are associated with some Melanesians. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
xa: Range: **Australia** and **Australian Melanesia**.
**Proto-Australoids** in India: **Munda, Santhal, Bhil**.
Proto-Australoid traits: **long head**, **depressed nasal root**, broad flat nose.

66.s: Dark skin, woolly hair, short stature and a broad flat nose are traits of which racial type?
66.x: These are the diagnostic traits of the Negrito; Proto-Australoids have wavy hair and a depressed nasal root.
66.tq: one-liner

66.s: In the 2009 genetic framework of Indian ancestry, what is the full form of 'ASI'?
66.x: Most Indians are described as a mixture of ANI (Ancestral North Indians) and ASI (Ancestral South Indians).
xa: ⚠ ASI here = Ancestral South Indians, not the archaeology body that gave **Rakhigarhi** skeletons to AnSI.
**Rakhigarhi** DNA showed **no "Steppe Pastoralist" gene**.
**Hutton** (**1931**): India peopled by successive waves of migration.

66.s: In Risley's classification, with which region is the 'Dravidian' type associated?
o: The Himalayan and north-eastern hills only
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands only
North-west India and the Punjab only
66.x: Risley used ‘Dravidian’ for South India and Chota Nagpur. In linguistic usage, however, Dravidian properly denotes a language family.
66.tq: Distinguish Risley’s geographical racial label from the later linguistic meaning of Dravidian.
xs: Risley's **Dravidian** type = **South India and Chota Nagpur** (and central India) — option **(1)** is correct.
BPSC **2016** key: Dravidian races confined to **South India**.
Himalaya and NE = Risley's **Mongoloid**; NW = **Turko-Iranian**/**Indo-Aryan**.
xa: Dravidian traits: **long head, broad nose, dark skin**; e.g. **Paniyan, Santals**.
'Dravidian' properly names a **language family**.
India's two main ethno-linguistic groups = **Indo-Aryan** + **Dravidian**.

66.s: Which one of the following Risley racial types is associated with Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier Province?
66.x: The Turko-Iranian type was associated with Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier region.
66.tq: Match the regional distribution with the correct Risley type.
xs: **Turko-Iranian** = **Baluchistan** and **NWFP** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Indo-Aryan** = Punjab, Rajasthan, Kashmir; **Aryo-Dravidian** = UP, Bihar; **Mongolo-Dravidian** = Bengal, Odisha.
xa: **Scytho-Dravidian** = Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Coorg.
**Mongoloid** = Himalaya, Assam and NE.
**Dravidian** = South India, Chota Nagpur, central India.

66.s: Under Risley's classification, Punjab, Rajasthan and Kashmir were associated with which type?
66.x: Risley linked Punjab, Rajasthan and Kashmir to the Indo-Aryan type; Scytho-Dravidian was linked to western India (Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Coorg).
xa: **Turko-Iranian** = Baluchistan, NWFP.
**Aryo-Dravidian** = **UP, Bihar**.
Risley gave **7** types.

66.s: How many racial types did Risley's classification of the Indian population have?
66.x: Risley gave seven types; Guha gave six main groups (with nine sub-types).
xa: Guha used **1931** Census data; Risley the **1901** Census.
Risley's types include **Turko-Iranian, Indo-Aryan, Scytho-Dravidian, Aryo-Dravidian, Mongolo-Dravidian, Mongoloid, Dravidian**.
Guha's is the **most widely cited** classification.

66.s: H.H. Risley was the Census Commissioner for which census and wrote which book?
o: Census of 1931; The Races of India
Census of 1901; The People of India
Census of 1881; The Tribes of India
66.x: H.H. Risley was the Census Commissioner for 1901 and wrote The People of India, published in 1908.
66.tq: Link the official position, census year and book title in one recall unit.
xs: **H.H. Risley** was Census Commissioner for **1901** and wrote **The People of India** (**1908**) — option **(3)** is correct.
He organised the **1901 ethnographic survey** and gave **7** racial types.
xa: ⚠ **People of India** project (**1985**) = **K.S. Singh**.
⚠ **Hutton** and **Guha** = **1931** Census.
Risley = exponent of the **racial theory of caste**.

66.s: With which of the following ideas is H.H. Risley associated?
66.x: Risley was the exponent of the racial theory of caste, which treats caste as a by-product of racial difference.
66.tq: Identify the scholar by his characteristic theory.
xs: **Risley** is linked with the **racial theory of caste** — option **(3)** is correct.
He saw caste as a **by-product of racial difference**.
xa: Dictum: caste status varies **inversely** with its **nasal index**.
Now rejected as **colonial race science**.
Risley gave **7** types; Guha **6** groups.

66.s: The older racial schemes of India have been criticised primarily because they relied heavily on
o: visible physical traits and colonial ethnography
66.x: Older schemes relied on visible traits and colonial ethnography. Risley's race-caste theory is now rejected.
66.tq: Identify the stated basis of the criticised classification rather than its later scientific alternative.
xs: Old racial schemes rested on **visible physical traits** and **colonial ethnography** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Risley**'s race-caste theory, built on the **nasal index**, is rejected.
xa: Modern science **rejects ranking by race**.
Anthropometric race typologies (Risley) are **discredited**.
All humans share **over 99%** of genetic material.

66.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Risley's dictum?
o: It linked the social status of a caste with its nasal index
It stated an inverse relationship between caste status and nasal index
It treated a higher nasal index as indicating higher social status
It is now rejected as colonial race science
66.x: The dictum said caste status varied inversely with nasal index, so a higher nasal index did not indicate higher status.

Consider the following statements about 'People of India':
1. The book The People of India (1908) was written by H.H. Risley.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

66.s: In Risley's classification, which racial type was found in Western India – Maharashtra, Saurashtra and Coorg?
66.x: Risley placed western India (Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Coorg) under the Scytho-Dravidian type.

66.s: Which racial type did Risley assign to Lower Bengal and Odisha?
66.x: Risley's Mongolo-Dravidian type covered Lower Bengal and Odisha.

66.s: Uttar Pradesh and Bihar were placed by Risley under which racial type?
66.x: Risley's Aryo-Dravidian type covered Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and parts of Rajasthan.

66.s: On which physical index did H.H. Risley mainly base his racial classification?
66.x: Risley used the nasal index; Sarkar used the cephalic index and Haddon hair form.

66.s: The term 'Dravidian', used by Risley as a racial type, properly names which of the following?
66.x: Dravidian is properly the name of a language family, like Indo-Aryan, not a race.

66.s: The Parsis have been placed under which racial type and sub-type respectively?
66.x: The Parsis are associated with the Western Brachycephal group and are identified with the Armenoid sub-type.
66.tq: Use the community-subtype pairing to avoid confusing broad racial groups with their sub-types.
xs: **Parsis** = **Western Brachycephal**, **Armenoid** sub-type — option **(3)** is correct.
Western Brachycephal sub-types: **Alpinoid, Dinaric, Armenoid**.
xa: Western Brachycephals are broad-headed: **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka (Coorg), Bengal-Odisha**.
**Tibeto-Mongoloid** = Tibetans of Sikkim.
**Andamanese** = Negrito.

66.s: Palaeo-Mediterranean, Mediterranean and Oriental are sub-types of which one of Guha's racial groups?
66.x: The Mediterranean group was divided into Palaeo-Mediterranean, Mediterranean and Oriental. The Oriental sub-type was associated with Punjab and Rajasthan.
66.tq: Match the sub-type cluster with its parent group.
xs: **Palaeo-Mediterranean, Mediterranean, Oriental** are sub-types of Guha's **Mediterranean** group — option **(2)** is correct.
Western Brachycephals = **Alpinoid, Dinaric, Armenoid**.
xa: Palaeo-Mediterranean = **south** (Dravidian-speaking); Mediterranean = **north**; Oriental = **Punjab, Rajasthan**.
AP's plains population is mainly **Mediterranean (Dravidian-speaking)**.
Mongoloid sub-types: **Palaeo-Mongoloid, Tibeto-Mongoloid**.

66.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Western Brachycephals — Gujarat, Bengal, Odisha and Coorg
Negrito — Punjab, Rajasthan and the Ganga plain
Mediterranean — Punjab, Rajasthan and the Ganga plain
66.x: The Negrito type is associated mainly with the Andaman Islands and traces in the southern hills. Punjab, Rajasthan and the Ganga plain are associated with the Mediterranean type, while Punjab and Rajasthan are also linked with the Nordic type.
66.tq: Find the geographical association that does not belong to the racial type.
xs: **Negrito — Punjab, Rajasthan, Ganga plain** is wrong — option **(3)** is correct.
Negritos live in the **Andaman Islands**, with traces in the far-south hills.
**Nordic** = Punjab, Rajasthan; **Western Brachycephals** = Gujarat, Bengal-Odisha, Coorg; **Mediterranean** = Punjab, Rajasthan, Ganga plain.
xa: **Palaeo-Mediterranean** = Dravidian-speaking south.
Western Brachycephals also in **Maharashtra**, **Karnataka**.
Nordic = **NW Frontier** too.

66.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Negrito – Onge, Jarawa and Great Andamanese
Proto-Australoid – Nagas, Lepchas and Tibetans of Sikkim
Mongoloid – Shompen and Tibetans of Sikkim
Nordic – Punjab, Rajasthan and North-West Frontier
66.x: Nagas, Lepchas and Tibetans of Sikkim are Mongoloid; the Proto-Australoid group is represented by Santhal, Bhil, Chenchu, Munda and Ho.
xa: Mongoloid: **Palaeo-Mongoloid** (Sema Nagas, Lepchas) and **Tibeto-Mongoloid** (Tibetans of Sikkim).
Nordic: **tall, fair, long-headed**.
⚠ **Shompen** are Mongoloid, unlike the Negrito **Jarawa, Onge**.

66.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched under B.S. Guha's classification?
o: Western Brachycephals — Alpinoid, Dinaric and Armenoid
Proto-Australoid — Munda, Santhal, Oraon, Bhil and Chenchu
66.x: Kadar and Irula are associated with the Negrito group. The Nordic group was associated with the north-west frontier and Punjab.
66.tq: Identify the representative population assigned to the wrong racial group.
xs: **Nordic — Kadar and Irula** is wrong — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kadar** and **Irula** carry **Negrito** traces; Nordic are the tall, fair people of the **north-west**.
The other pairs are correct.
xa: Negrito strain among southern hill foragers: **Kadar, Irula, Paniyan**.
Nordic region: **Punjab, Rajasthan, NW Frontier**.
**Proto-Australoid** also includes **Ho**.

66.s: The Chenchus of the Nallamala region are generally classified under which racial group?
66.x: The Chenchus of the Nallamala region are classified as Proto-Australoid.
66.tq: Use the tribe’s regional location and standard classification together.
xs: The **Chenchus** of the **Nallamala** are **Proto-Australoid** — option **(2)** is correct.
Most central and south Indian tribes, incl. AP's, are **Proto-Australoid**.
xa: AP plains population = **Mediterranean (Dravidian-speaking)**.
Negrito examples (**Kadar, Irula**) are in southern hills **beyond AP**.

66.s: B.S. Guha's racial classification of the Indian population was based on the data of which Census?

68.s: Identify the incorrect statement on the linguistic diversity of India:

68.s: With reference to India, the terms 'Halbi, Ho and Kui' pertain to
68.x: Halbi, also known as Bastari, is an Eastern Indo-Aryan language spoken by various tribes in central India. Ho, a tribal language, is written in the Warang Chiti script and is the mother tongue of nearly a million tribal people in Odisha and Jharkhand. The Kandhas communicate through Kui, a South-Eastern Dravidian language primarily spoken in Odisha and documented in the Odia script. The Kui language was also referred to as the Kuinga language during the historical period. It is closely related to the Gondi and Kuvi languages.

68.s: The Dravidian races are mainly confined to which of the following parts of India?
68.x: The Dravidian races are mainly confined to South India. This race is related to the Dravidian language family, which includes Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Telugu, etc. They are also found in central and southeast India.

68.s: Which one of the following languages belongs to the Austric group?
68.x: The languages of Austric group (Austro-Asiatic) are Khasi, Santhali, Mundari and Bhumij etc. It is a language spoken by the Indian tribes.

68.s: Which one of the following is the largest linguistic group of India?

68.s: The Munda language group belongs to which family?
68.x: Munda languages (Santhali, Mundari, Ho, Savara) belong to the Austro-Asiatic (Austric) family, so Austric is correct.

68.s: Which of the following is not the language of Bastar region?
68.x: Gondi, Halbi and Bhatri are spoken in the Bastar region, whereas Sadari is not a Bastar language; the notes do not state this directly.

68.x: Indian languages fall into four main families: Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic and Sino-Tibetan, so the answer is Four.

xs: **Dardic** (incl. **Kashmiri**) is **Indo-Aryan** — option **(4)** is correct.

xa: Dardic is spoken in **J&K**.

Sino-Tibetan includes **Manipuri, Bodo, Bhotia, Garo**.

xa: Munda: **Santhali, Mundari, Ho, Savara**; Mon-Khmer: **Khasi, Nicobarese**.
Areas: **Jharkhand-Odisha-WB** tribal belt, **Meghalaya**, **Nicobar Islands**.
Share about **1.1-1.4%**.

Consider the following statements:
1. Recently, all the countries of the United Nations have adopted the first-ever compact for international migration, the 'Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM)'.
2. The objectives and commitments stated in the GCM are binding on the UN member countries.

How many of the above statements are correct?
69.x: All statements are incorrect: The Global Compact on Migration is the first-ever UN global agreement on a common approach to international migration in all its dimensions. On December 19, 2018, the United Nations General Assembly officially endorsed the compact through a vote, with 152 countries supporting the resolution (not all countries). It is of a non-legally binding nature. It is intended to: Address all aspects of international migration, including the humanitarian, developmental, human rights-related and other aspects;  Make an important contribution to global governance and enhance coordination on international migration;  Present a framework for comprehensive international cooperation on migrants and human mobility; International Relations PMF IAS Misc – 47  Set out a range of actionable commitments, means of implementation and a framework for follow-up and review among Member States regarding international migration in all its dimensions;  Be guided by the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Addis Ababa Action Agenda; and  Be informed by the Declaration of the 2013 High-Level Dialogue on International Migration and Development. • The GCM is primarily focused on international migration and does not directly address internal migration or the situation of internally displaced persons. PMF Concept Hack: Statement 1 can be eliminated because the phrase "all the countries of the United Nations" is a classic UPSC trap. International agreements and compacts

69.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Recently, all the countries of the United Nations have adopted the first-ever compact for international migration, the ‘Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM)’.
2. The objectives and commitments stated in the GCM are binding on the UN member countries.
3. The GCM addresses internal migration or internally displaced people also in its objectives and commitments.
How many of the above statements are correct?
69.x: The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration is the first intergovernmental agreement, adopted under the auspices of the United Nations, to cover all dimensions of international migration in a holistically and comprehensive manner. It was adopted at an intergovernmental conference on migration in Marrakesh, Morocco, on 10 December 2018. At the ceremony to adopt the text on 10 December, only 163 countries formally adopted it. Further, countries like Austria were critical of it and refrained from adopting it in 2018. Hence statement 1 is not correct. The Global Compact for Migration is the first-ever UN global agreement on a common approach to international migration in all its dimensions. The global compact is non-legally binding. Hence, statement 2 is not correct. The Global Compact enumerates 23 objectives for State action, bolstered by specific commitments, that seek to address challenges related to today’s migration. The GCM commitments and actions can be seen as a guide for States to meet their human rights obligations when designing migration governance measures to reduce the risks and vulnerabilities migrants face at different stages of migration and to create conducive conditions that empower all migrants to become active members of society. Key commitments include: Strengthening evidence-based and human rights-based policy-making and public discourse on migration; Minimizing the adverse drivers of migration, including combating poverty and discrimination

79.s:

79.s: To which of the following sectors of the economy, the activity of agriculture and services belong to?
79.x: Agriculture is a primary activity (direct use of nature), while services such as transport, trade and banking are tertiary, so the answer is primary and tertiary respectively.

79.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
79.x: Cement manufacturing is a secondary-sector activity. Transport is tertiary, research and development is quaternary, and top decision-making is quinary.
79.tq: Use the activity-to-sector match and watch for neighbouring-sector substitutions.
xs: **Cement manufacturing** is a **secondary sector** activity — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Transport** is **tertiary** (APPSC-GS 2018 key); **research and development** is **quaternary**; top government decision-making is **quinary**.
xa: Primary = **agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining and quarrying** (direct use of nature).
Quaternary also covers **IT, education, consulting** (knowledge).
Quinary workers are called "**gold collar**".

79.s: By the nature of the activity, to which sector does mining belong, though GVA reporting places it in the Industry sector?
79.x: Mining is primary because it extracts resources from nature; in GVA reporting it is grouped under Industry.
xa: The **APPSC-G2 2008** key left this question unanswered.
Mining is an **extractive industry**, like capture fishing, hunting and lumbering.

79.s: Transport belongs to which sector of the economy?
79.x: Transport is a service, hence tertiary (APPSC 2018), not secondary.

79.s: To which sector does top decision-making by government and top executives belong?

79.s: Research and development belongs to which sector?

79.s: Stock Farming is –
o: Growing of 2-3 crops at the same time
79.x: Stock farming is the practice of keeping livestock farm. Animal Husbandry is the scientific management of animal livestock. It includes various aspect such as feeding, breeding and disease control. Thus (b) is the correct answer.

79.s: Which human activity is most affected by climate?
79.x: Farming depends most directly on climate (rainfall, temperature, seasons) for crop growth. Fishing and mining are less climate-dependent and manufacturing least of all.

79.s: Which of the following pairs represents the oldest primary activities?
79.x: Hunting and gathering are regarded as the oldest primary activities because they involve direct dependence on nature for subsistence.
79.tq: Identify the historically earliest activities through their direct dependence on nature.
xs: **Hunting and gathering** are the **oldest primary activities** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Manufacturing is secondary; banking and trade tertiary; research and consulting quaternary.
xa: **Extractive industries** take what nature provides: **mining, capture fishing, hunting, lumbering**.
**Genetic industries** breed plants and animals: **agriculture**, animal husbandry, fish farming.

79.s: Which one of the following is NOT an extractive industry?

**Capture fishing, mining, lumbering** (and hunting) are **extractive** — they take what nature provides.
xa: Genetic industries: **agriculture**, animal husbandry, **fish farming** (UPPSC 2016 key: **Agriculture**).
⚠ **Capture fishing** = extractive, but **fish farming** = genetic.

79.s: Animal husbandry is classified as which type of primary activity?
79.x: Animal husbandry breeds animals, so it is a genetic industry, not extractive.

79.s: Which sector accounted for the largest share of India’s GVA in 2024–25, on the new 2022–23 base?

**45.6%** is AP's **agriculture employment** share (PLFS 2023-24), not India's GVA.

79.s: According to the Fisher-Clark thesis, in which order do labour and output move during structural transformation?
79.x: The thesis states that as income rises, labour and output generally move from the primary sector to the secondary sector and then to the tertiary sector.

80.s:
With reference to primitive subsistence agricultural practices, which of the pair/s is/are correctly matched? Agricultural Practices Region
1. Jhumming : South-East Asia
2. Milpa : Mexico
3. Ladang : Sri Lanka
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
80.x: Primitive subsistence agricultural practices : Jhumming - South East Asia Milpa - Mexico and Central America Ladang - Indonesia Hence statements 1 and 2 are correct. Primitive subsistence agricultural practices are also called slash and burn farming methods, which are prevalent in many tribes of the world including India. 54. Assertion (A) : A plant which has Nitrogen deficiency will show symptoms like stunted growth and pale green and yellow leaves. Reason (R) : Nitrogen is responsible for green leaf growth. (a) Both (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). (b) Both (A) are (R) are individually true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). (c) (A) is true, but (R) is false. (d) (A) is false, but (R) is true. M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2008 Ans. (a) Nitrogen is an essential element for the growth and development of plants. It is a major constituent for the formation of cells and tissues. Due to a lack of nitrogen, the development of plants is blocked. The chlorophyll content of the plant leaves is reduced which results in a pale yellow color. Older leaves turn completely yellow. Flowering, fruiting, protein and starch contents are reduced. A reduction in protein results in stunted growth and dormant lateral buds.

80.s: What is 'Jhum'?
o: The name of a river valley
80.x: Jhuming is a type of shifting cultivation that is done by the tribes by clearing the forests. When fertility of that place degrades they shift to another place and the same procedure is followed again and again.

80.s: Slash and burn agriculture, commonly called as Jhum cultivation is practiced in the-
80.x: Slash and burn agriculture, commonly called as Jhum cultivation practiced in the North eastern states of India like Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland, Tripura, Sikkim Pamlou in Manipur etc. Slash and burn agriculture, formers clear a patch of land and produce cerals and other food crops to sustain their family. When the Soil Fertility decrease, the farmers shift and clear a fresh patch of land for cultivation. This type of shifting allows nature to replenish the fertilify of the soil through natural process, land productivity in this type of agriculture is low as the farmer does not use fertiliser or other modern inputs.

80.s: Which of the following is the chief characteristic of 'mixed farming'?
o: Cultivation of both cash crops and food crops
Cultivation of two or more crops in the same field
Rearing of animals and cultivation of crops together
80.x: Mixed farming involves growing crops alongside livestock operations. It has several advantages: • Optimum diversity may be obtained by integrating crops and livestock in the same farming operation. • Growing crops only on more level land and pastures or forages on steeper slopes will reduce soil erosion. • Pasture and leguminous forage crops in rotation enhance soil quality and reduce erosion; livestock manure, in turn, contributes to soil fertility. Indian Agriculture PMF IAS Misc – 12 • Livestock can buffer the negative impacts of low rainfall periods by consuming crop residue, which in "plant only" systems would have been considered crop failure. • Feeding and marketing are flexible in animal production systems. This can help cushion farmers against price fluctuations and make more efficient use of farm labour

Statement: Sequential cropping involves planting multiple crops in a sequence on the same field within a year, without intercrop competition. Intercropping leads to crop intensification in both time and space dimensions, with competition between crops during their growth stages. Sole cropping is the practice of growing a single crop variety on a field, not multiple varieties simultaneously. The Land Equivalent Ratio (LER) is used to measure the productivity advantage of intercropping compared to sole cropping.
Conclusion: The correct practice for measuring the productivity of intercropping in comparison to sole cropping is the use of the Land Equivalent Ratio (LER).
Which of the following can be drawn from the above statement?

A) Sequential cropping and intercropping both involve growing multiple crops on the same field simultaneously.

B) Sole cropping refers to growing a single crop variety, not multiple varieties.

C) The Land Equivalent Ratio (LER) measures the productivity of sequential cropping.

D) Intercropping has no impact on the productivity of the land.

82.x: Pepper requires a hot and humid climate with high rainfall, usually above 150 centimetres annually. It grows well on hill slopes up to about 1000 to 1200 metres, especially in the Western Ghats region. The temperature range of 15 to 30 degrees Celsius is ideal for pepper cultivation. Thrives in well-drained, deep loamy soils rich in organic matter (humus). It also grows in red laterite, red loam, and sandy loam soils. Prefers slightly acidic soil with a pH range of 5.5 to 6.5.

82.s: The lower Gangetic plain is characterised by a humid climate with high temperature throughout the year. Which one among the following pairs of crops is most suitable for this region?
82.x: The Lower Gangetic Plain, located in the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta region, experiences a humid climate with high temperatures and heavy rainfall (around 1700 mm or more). The region frequently experiences flooding, and the rivers deposit fertile alluvial silt, making the soil extremely productive. These conditions are highly suitable for paddy cultivation, as rice requires abundant water, warm temperatures, and fertile alluvial soil. The region is also ideal for jute cultivation. Jute grows best in warm, humid climates with heavy rainfall and fertile alluvial soils. Indian Agriculture PMF IAS Misc – 22 The annual deposition of fresh silt by floods in the delta region further enriches the soil, creating ideal conditions for producing high-quality jute.

Indian Agriculture PMF IAS Misc – 18 • While cotton can tolerate some salinity, it is highly vulnerable to waterlogging. As a Kharif crop, cotton requires 6 to 8 months to mature. Adequate water needs can be met with an annual rainfall of 50-100 cm, but successful cultivation is also achievable in regions with lower rainfall through irrigation.

86.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

86.tq: Classify industries by weight change and location tendency.
xs: **Sugar** is a **raw-material-based** industry — so option **(1)** is correct: sugarcane is **perishable** and the input is **weight-losing**.
**Bakery** is **market-based** (weight-gaining or fragile products, located near consumers).
**Iron and steel** is raw-material-based (about **4 t** of input per tonne), and **cement** is raw-material-based on **limestone** — neither is market-based or footloose.
xa: **Power-oriented**: **aluminium**, needing **14,000-15,000 kWh** per tonne.
**Footloose** examples: **software**, **electronics**, and **cotton textiles** (cotton is a "pure" material).
⚠ Both **sugar** and **iron & steel** are weight-losing, so Weber puts them near raw material (**MI > 1**).

86.s: Market-based industries are generally located near consumers because their products are:

86.tq: Apply the product-characteristic test to market location.
xs: Market-based industries locate near consumers because their products are **weight-gaining or fragile** — option **(3)**.
Examples given: **bakery** and **soft drinks**.
**Weight-losing and perishable** inputs describe **raw-material-oriented** industries (sugar, iron & steel, cement), not market-based ones.
Dependence on cheap electricity is **power orientation** (aluminium).
xa: In Weber's theory, **MI < 1** or **ubiquitous inputs** (such as **water**) pull an industry **near the market**.
**Footloose** industries locate anywhere with **skills and links** — software, electronics, diamond polishing.
Location factors include **raw material**, **power**, **market**, **labour**, **transport**, water and **government policy**.

86.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Alfred Weber's least-cost theory?
o: A Material Index above 1 pulls the industry towards the market

86.x: MI above 1 (weight-losing inputs, e.g. iron and steel, sugar) pulls the plant to the raw material, not the market.
xa: **Pure raw material** (no weight loss, e.g. **cotton**) → free to locate anywhere.
**Footloose** = **software / diamond** (APPSC **2019**).
Steel needs about **4 t** of input per tonne.

86.s: In Weber's least-cost theory, where can an industry using a 'pure' raw material such as cotton, which loses no weight in processing, be located?
o: Anywhere between the source and the market
86.x: A pure raw material has no weight loss, so transport cost is the same whether raw material or product is moved; the plant is free to locate anywhere between source and market. Weight-losing inputs (MI > 1) pull it to the source (A); weight-gaining or ubiquitous inputs (MI < 1) pull it to the market (B); a port location (D) is not implied by the theory.
86.tq: Pure material (cotton) = free location; weight-losing = source; ubiquitous = market.
xs: A **pure raw material** such as **cotton** loses no weight, so the plant can locate **anywhere between the source and the market** — option **(3)**.
**Weight-losing** inputs (**MI > 1**) pull the plant to the raw-material source.
**MI < 1** or ubiquitous inputs (water) pull it to the market.
xa: This is why **cotton textiles** are listed as **footloose** in the orientation table.
**Alfred Weber (1909)**: least total transport cost first, then labour and agglomeration adjustments.
Iron & steel needs about **4 t** of input per tonne — a classic weight-losing case.

95.s: Which is the longest canal of commercial importance in Andhra?
95.x:
The Buckingham Canal is the longest navigation canal on the eastern coast of India and the most important canal of commercial significance in Andhra Pradesh. Constructed during the British period, the canal extends for about 796 km, running parallel to the Coromandel Coast from Andhra Pradesh to Tamil Nadu. It connected several important ports and facilitated the transport of rice, salt, timber, textiles and agricultural produce before the development of railways and highways. In Andhra Pradesh, the canal connected important centres such as Kakinada, Eluru, Machilipatnam and Nellore, making it a vital route for inland water transport. Although the K.C. Canal, Bandar Canal and Eluru Canal are important irrigation canals, they do not possess the same commercial and navigational significance as the Buckingham Canal. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Longest Navigation Canal – Buckingham Canal
• Length – Approximately 796 km
• Importance – Inland navigation and commercial transport

99.x: Statement 1 is incorrect: Some coal-fired thermal power plants in India use seawater for cooling. For example, situated in Gujarat's Kutch district, the Mundra Thermal Power Station ranks as India's second-largest, boasting a capacity of 4,620MW. Primarily fueled by imported Indonesian coal, the plant draws seawater from the Gulf of Kutch. Statement 2 is incorrect: The World Resource Institute's (WRI) report finds that 40 per cent of the country's thermal power plants are located in areas facing high water stress, a problem since these plants use water for cooling. The report says, "scarce water is already hampering electricity generation in these regions—14 of India's 20 largest thermal utilities experienced at least one shutdown due to water shortages between 2013 and 2016, costing the companies $1.4 billion''. Almost 90 per cent of India's thermal power generation depends on freshwater for cooling. Statement 3 is incorrect: There are many privately owned coal-based thermal power plants. 99.s: Where was the first nuclear power station established in the world?
99.x: The pursuit of nuclear energy for electricity generation began soon after the discovery in the early 20th century that radioactive elements, such as radium, released an immense amount of energy, according to the principle of mass-energy equivalence. In 1932, James Chadwick discovered the neutron, which was immediately recognized as a potential tool for nuclear experimentation because of its lack of an electric charge. Experimentation with a bombardment of materials with neutrons led Frederic and Irene Juliut-Curie to discover induced radioactivity in 1934, which allowed the creation of radium-like elements at much less the price of natural radium. Further work by Enrico Fermi in the 1930s focused on using slow neutrons to increase the effectiveness of induced radioactivity. In the United States, where Fermi and Szilárd had both emigrated, this led to the creation of the first man-made reactor, known as Chicago Pile-1, which was successfully operated on December 2, 1942. This work became part of the Manhattan Project, which made enriched uranium and built large reactors to breed plutonium for use in the first nuclear weapons, which were used on the cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Electricity was generated for the first time by a nuclear reactor on December 20, 1951, at the EBR-I (Experimental Breeder Reactor-1) experimental station near Arco, Idaho,USA which initially produced about 100 kW.Thus, option (d) is the correct answer.
